title.raw: 卷二十六 志第十六 食貨 Volume 26 Treatises 16: Finance and Economics

sentences.zh: 昔者先王量地以制邑，度地以居民，因三才以節其務，敬四序以成其業，觀其謠俗而正其紀綱。

translations.literal: In antiquity the former kings measured land to regulate settlements, surveyed land to settle the people, guided their tasks according to the three powers (Heaven, Earth, and Man), honored the four seasons to complete their undertakings, and inspected local songs and customs to set right law and discipline.
translations.idiomatic: The kings of old sized out territory to lay out towns, reckoned acreage to house the people, tuned their duties to the triad of Heaven, earth, and mankind, kept faith with the turning year to finish each season's work, and read popular sentiment so they could straighten what statute and custom required.

sentences.zh: 勖農桑之本，通魚鹽之利，登良山而采符玉，泛瀛海而罩珠璣。

translations.literal: They urged the root of farming and sericulture, opened access to the profit of fish and salt, climbed worthy hills to gather tally-jade, and sailed the Eastern Sea to seine pearls and precious beads.
translations.idiomatic: They promoted tillage and silk as the economy's foundation, extended trade in fish and salt, scaled high hills for ritual jade, and crossed the deep sea to harvest pearls.

sentences.zh: 日中為市，總天下之隸，先諸布帛，繼以貨泉，貿遷有無，各得其所。

translations.literal: They held market at midday, assembling all the laborers of the realm; first came cloth and silk, then currency; they traded surplus for want so that each found his proper place.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun stood at the meridian they opened the mart, drawing workers from across the land—first with bolts of cloth, then with coined cash—swapping abundance for scarcity until buyer and seller were matched.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》，正月始和，乃布教于象魏。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou says: In the first month, when harmony begins, they promulgated instruction at the Elephant Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhouli records that with the new year's first month they proclaimed the royal teachings beneath the watch-towers flanking the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 若乃一夫之士，十畝之宅，三日之徭，九均之賦，施陽禮以興其讓，命春社以勖其耕。

translations.literal: Where one husbandman held his allotment, a homestead of ten mu, three days of corvée, and the ninefold equitable levy, they applied the 'yang' rites to encourage yielding deference and ordered the spring she sacrifice to spur plowing.
translations.idiomatic: Each farmer had his plot and homestead, a short stint of labor service, and the graded land tax; ritual taught humility, and the spring communal feast kept everyone at the plough.

sentences.zh: 天之所貴者人也，明之所求者學也，治《經》入官，則君子之道焉。

translations.literal: What Heaven esteems is human beings; what enlightened rule seeks is learning; mastering the Classics and entering office—that is the way of the gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven prizes humanity; good government prizes scholarship; the path of the junzi runs through the canon and into service.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「三之日於耜，四之日舉趾。

translations.literal: The Odes says: 'On the third month they sharpen the plough-shares; on the fourth month they raise their feet [to walk to the fields].'
translations.idiomatic: As the Book of Songs puts it, in the third month they hone the shared blade; in the fourth they stride out to the furrows.

sentences.zh: 」是以農官澤虞，各有攸次，父兄之習，不玩而成，十五從務，始勝衣服，鄉無遊手，邑不廢時，所謂厥初生民，各從其事者也。

translations.literal: Therefore the agricultural and forestry officials each held his station; the customs of fathers and elders were perfected without idle amusement; at fifteen they undertook labor and first wore full adult dress; in the hamlets none wandered idle, in the towns the seasons were not wasted—this is what is meant by 'when the people first arose, each followed his proper task.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence field overseers and marsh wardens stood in fixed posts; household instruction hardened young hands without play; at fifteen youths took up work and adult clothes; villages held no loafers and towns lost no farming window—that was the world in which, as the ode says, each newborn generation stuck to its calling.

sentences.zh: 是以太公通市井之貨，以致齊國之強；

translations.literal: Thus the Grand Duke opened the circulation of market goods and thereby brought strength to the state of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: That is how Jiang Taigong turned ward and marketplace into strength for Qi.

sentences.zh: 鴟夷善發斂之居，以盛中陶之業。

translations.literal: Lord Chiyi excelled at the depots for fiscal collection; thereby he magnified the pottery industry of the central heartland.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Li, styled Lord Chiyi, knew how to marshal stores and levies, and so he built up the great pottery workshops of the interior.

sentences.zh: 昔在金天，勤於民事，命春鳸以耕稼，召夏鳸以耘鋤，秋鳸所以收斂，冬鳸于焉蓋藏。

translations.literal: Long ago, in the reign associated with Jin Tian, he was diligent in the people's tasks: he appointed the spring bird-officer for plowing and sowing, summoned the summer bird-officer for weeding and hoeing, relied on the autumn bird-officer for gathering the harvest, and assigned the winter bird-officer for laying grain by.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shaohao's 'Metal Heaven' line, every season had its bird-titled minister—spring for seeding, summer for weeding, autumn for reaping, winter for storage—so the calendar never slipped.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「曆象日月星辰，敬授民時。

translations.literal: The Documents says: 'We calculated and aligned the sun, moon, and stars, and reverently gave the people their seasons.'
translations.idiomatic: The Shangshu counsels men to chart sun, moon, and stars and hand peasants a trustworthy calendar.

sentences.zh: 」傳曰：「禹稷躬稼而有天下。

translations.literal: The tradition says: 'Yu and Hou Ji personally farmed and thereby gained the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: Tradition adds that Yu and the Lord Millet tilled their own soil—and thus earned the mandate.

sentences.zh: 」若乃九土既敷，四民承范，東吳有齒角之饒，西蜀有丹沙之富，兗豫漆絲之廥，燕齊怪石之府，秦邠旄羽，迥帶琅玕，荊郢桂林，旁通竹箭，江幹橘柚，河外舟車，遼西旃罽之鄉，蔥右蒲梢之駿，殖物怪錯，於何不有。

translations.literal: When the nine provinces had been laid out and the four peoples received their models, eastern Wu had abundance in ivory and horn, western Shu hoarded cinnabar, Yan and Henan barns brimmed with lacquer and silk, Yan and Qi quarried strange stones, Qin and Bin offered yak tails and kingfisher feathers strung with carnelian, Jing, Ying, and Guilin shipped bamboo arrows, river terraces grew oranges and pomelos, beyond the Yellow River ran boats and carts, Liaoxi was home to felts and rugs, and past the Cong ranges came the famed Pu-shao horses—products multiplied bewilderingly; what was there that could not be found?
translations.idiomatic: Once the nine domains were mapped and the four classes knew their trades, the southeast traded ivory, Bashu poured out cinnabar, Yan-Yu warehoused lacquer thread, Qi quarried odd stone, the northwest sent feathers and jade trinkets, the middle Yangzi routed bamboo, riverbanks fattened citrus, the Grand Canal moved freight, the far northeast shipped wool, and the western steppe sent horses—goods crossed every boundary imaginable.

sentences.zh: 若乃上法星象，下料無外，因天地之利，而總山海之饒，百畝之田，十一而稅，九年躬稼，而有三年之蓄，可以長孺齒，可以養耆年。

translations.literal: When they took pattern from the stars above and omitted nothing in surveying below, relying on heaven-and-earth profit and gathering the bounty of mountains and seas, for fields of one hundred mu they levied one part in ten; after nine years of the ruler personally farming they laid up three years' surplus—thereby they could nurture the young and sustain the aged.
translations.idiomatic: Taking cues from the sky and leaving no acre unmeasured on earth, pooling hill and sea wealth, titheing one tenth off each hundred-mu farm, and insisting that nine harvest years include three years of reserves—that was how children grew strong and elders were fed.

sentences.zh: 因乎人民，用之邦國，宮室有度，旗章有序。

translations.literal: Applied among the people and deployed in the feudal states, palace chambers kept their degrees of rank, flags and emblems kept their proper sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Carried into hamlet and kingdom, it fixed how high halls might rise and how banners should march in order.

sentences.zh: 朝聘自其儀，宴饗由其制，家殷國阜，遠至邇安。

translations.literal: Court audiences and diplomatic missions followed their ritual forms; feasts and communal drinks followed their regulations; households grew rich and the state prosperous, the distant submitted and the near rested secure.
translations.idiomatic: Embassies and banquets each had rule-books; wealth filled granaries while neighbors stayed calm.

sentences.zh: 救水旱之災，恤寰瀛之弊，然後王之常膳，乃間笙鏞。

translations.literal: They relieved flood and drought disasters and aided distress throughout the realm; only after that did the king's ordinary meals occasionally borrow meat from the bell-and-chime orchestra.
translations.idiomatic: They drained floods, eased drought, and patched every coastland hurt by scarcity—only then did the throne dine with leisure enough to hear bronze bells.

sentences.zh: 商周之興，用此道也。

translations.literal: The rise of Shang and Zhou relied on this approach.
translations.idiomatic: Shang and Zhou rose by walking this same road.

sentences.zh: 辛紂暴虐，玩其經費，金鏤傾宮，廣延百里，玉飾鹿臺，崇高千仞，宮中九市，各有女司。

translations.literal: The tyrants Xin of Shang and Zhou were cruel and violent, squandering resources: the Qing Palace was overlaid with gold and stretched a hundred li; the Deer Terrace was faced with jade and rose a thousand ren; inside the palace stood nine markets, each supervised by women.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou of Shang and Di Xin wrecked the treasury on cruelty—gold sheathing for the tilted palace over endless leagues, jade facing for Deer Terrace up sheer cliffs, and nine separate markets inside the harem, each run by female clerks.

sentences.zh: 厚賦以實鹿臺之錢，大斂以增钜橋之粟，多發妖冶以充傾宮之麗，廣收珍玩以備沙丘之遊。

translations.literal: Heavy levies filled the coin stored at Deer Terrace; vast extractions swelled the grain at Great Bridge Granary; they collected hosts of seductive women to pack the tilted palace with beauty, and amassed rare treasures to supply the revels at Sand Dunes.
translations.idiomatic: Extortion stacked bronze at Deer Terrace, bulk grain at Juqiao, concubines for the leaning halls, and curios for the desert hunt.

sentences.zh: 懸肉成林，積醪為沼，使男女裸體相逐於其間，伏詣酒池中牛飲者三千餘人，宮中以錦綺為席，綾紈為薦。

translations.literal: They hung meat until it formed a forest and piled ale until it became a marsh; they made men and women chase one another naked within them; more than three thousand people lay prone along the ale pool and drank like cattle; inside the palace they used damask for mats and fine silk for cushions.
translations.idiomatic: Carcasses hung like a forest, wine pooled like a pond; stripped revelers chased one another while thousands flopped at the pool's lip and sucked wine like oxen; chambers were carpeted in brocade and padded with figured silk.

sentences.zh: 及周王誅紂，肅拜殷墟，乃盡振鹿財，並頒橋粟，上天降休，殷人大喜。

translations.literal: When the king of Zhou punished Zhou of Shang and reverently bowed amid the ruins of Yin, he shook out everything hoarded at Deer Terrace and distributed all the grain from Bridge Granary; Heaven sent its blessing, and the Yin people rejoiced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu smote the Shang king he emptied the Deer Terrace vaults, threw open Juqiao's granaries, and the conquered capital hailed heaven's mercy.

sentences.zh: 王赧云季，徙都西周，九鼎淪沒，二南堙盡，貸于百姓，無以償之，乃上層臺以避其責，周人謂王所居為逃責臺者也。

translations.literal: In the closing years of King Nan he moved the capital to western Zhou; the Nine Tripods sank from sight and the 'two southern' odes fell silent; he borrowed from the hundred surnames and could not repay, so he climbed a high terrace to dodge his creditors—the Zhou people called the king's residence the Debt-Fleeing Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: King Nan's late reign shifted the court west, lost the cauldrons, silenced the southern hymns, borrowed until bankruptcy, and hid on a platform locals mocked as the terrace for outrunning debt.

sentences.zh: 昔周姬公制以六典，職方陳其九貢，頒財內府，永為不刊。

translations.literal: Formerly the Duke of Zhou framed the six canons; the Office of Regions listed the nine tribute items; revenue entered the inner treasury and remained an unchanging statute.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou's six statutes—and the ninefold tribute schedule in the Zhou guan—fed the inner palace vault as permanent law.

sentences.zh: 及刑政陵夷，菁茅罕至，魯侯初踐畝之稅，秦君收太半之入，前王之範，靡有孑遺。

translations.literal: When punishments and government slackened, fine tribute grass seldom arrived; the lord of Lu first trod the tax on field yield; the lord of Qin took more than half the harvest; the models of former kings hardly survived.
translations.idiomatic: As government frayed, ritual bundles of thatch grew rare; Lu pioneered the acre tax, Qin seized over half the crop, and ancient fiscal norms vanished.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：班固為《殖貨志》，自三代至王莽之誅，網羅前載，其文詳悉。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Ban Gu composed the 'Treatise on Increasing Wealth,' spanning from the Three Dynasties down to the execution of Wang Mang; it gathers earlier records and its text is thorough.
translations.idiomatic: The editors comment: Ban Gu's 'Huozhi zhi' runs from the Xia-Shang-Zhou age to Wang Mang's fall, netting prior sources in exhaustive detail.

sentences.zh: 光武寬仁，龔行天討，王莽之後，赤眉新敗，雖復三暉乃眷，而九服蕭條，及得隴望蜀，黎民安堵，自此始行五銖之錢，田租三十稅一，民有產子者復以三年之算。

translations.literal: Guangwu was lenient and humane and marched as Heaven's avenger; after Wang Mang the Red Eyebrows had only just been defeated; although the three luminaries again smiled on the house of Han, the nine circuits lay desolate; only after he secured Long and still eyed Shu did common people settle in peace; from that point he began casting wushu cash, taxing fields at one thirtieth, and remitting the poll tax for three years for families who bore a child.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu's punitive mandate ended Wang Mang and the Red Eyebrows; even when Heaven still favored Han, the provinces were a wasteland until he pacified the northwest and no longer feared Shu—then subjects unpacked their bundles. He minted five-zhu coins, fixed the land rent at one part in thirty, and freed new parents from the head tax for three annual assessments.

sentences.zh: 顯宗即位，天下安寧，民無橫徭，歲比登稔。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended, the realm was peaceful; the people suffered no arbitrary corvée, and harvests year after year ripened full.
translations.idiomatic: Ming's accession brought quiet borders, no surprise levies, and full bins every autumn.

sentences.zh: 作常滿倉，立粟市於城東，粟斛直錢二十。

translations.literal: They built the Ever-Full Granary and established a grain market east of the capital; one hu of millet cost twenty cash.
translations.idiomatic: They stacked the Ever-Full Granary and sold grain east of the walls at twenty coins the hu.

sentences.zh: 草樹殷阜，牛羊彌望，作貢尤輕，府廩還積，奸回不用，禮義專行。

translations.literal: Grass and trees grew lush; cattle and sheep covered the horizon; tribute levies were especially light; granaries refilled; treachery found no purchase and ritual alone guided conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Verdant pasture fattened herds; taxes stayed mild; silos swelled; fraud faded while ritual carried the day.

sentences.zh: 于時東方既明，百官詣闕，戚裏侯家，自相馳騖，車如流水，馬若飛龍，照映軒廡，光華前載。

translations.literal: At that hour the east had brightened; the hundred officials hastened to court; kin of consorts and marquises' houses raced one another in display; carriages flowed like water, horses flew like dragons, glittering along galleries and outshining former generations.
translations.idiomatic: Dawn brought ministers to the gates while imperial in-laws vied in splendor—carriages streaming, horses wheeling, light dancing along the colonnades.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「三統之元，有陰陽之九焉」，蓋天地之恆數也。

translations.literal: The tradition says: 'At the inception of the Three Systems there are the nine configurations of yin and yang'—that is probably heaven and earth' constant reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient glosses hold that the Three Ages' opening counts nine permutations of yin and yang—the fixed mathematics of the cosmos.

sentences.zh: 安帝，天下水旱，人民相食。

translations.literal: Under Emperor An, flood and drought struck the realm and people devoured one another.
translations.idiomatic: An's reign drowned and parched the empire until men ate men.

sentences.zh: 帝以鴻陂之地假與貧民。

translations.literal: The emperor lent out the lands of the Hong marsh to poor commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The throne parcelled Hong Pool acreage to destitute farmers.

sentences.zh: 以用度不足，三公又奏請令吏民入錢穀得為關內侯云。

translations.literal: Because expenditures were insufficient, the three dukes jointly memorialized asking that officials and commoners be allowed to purchase rank as marquises within the passes by paying coin or grain.
translations.idiomatic: Short revenue drove the three excellencies to sell interior marquisates for cash or grain.

sentences.zh: 桓帝，郡國少半遭蝗，河泛數千里，流人十餘萬戶，所在廩給。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Huan, nearly half the commanderies and kingdoms suffered locusts; the Yellow River burst its banks for thousands of li; more than a hundred thousand households were displaced wanderers, but relief was issued wherever they halted.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's years brought locusts across half the provinces, a thousand-li flood on the Yellow River, and over a hundred thousand refugee households fed from state granaries.

sentences.zh: 迨建甯永和之初，西羌反叛，二十餘年兵連師老，軍旅之費三百二十餘億，府帑空虛，延及內郡。

translations.literal: By the opening years of Jianning and Yonghe, the western Qiang rebelled; for more than twenty years campaigns dragged on and armies aged; military costs surpassed 3.2 billion cash; the treasury emptied and distress spread into the interior commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jianning-Yonghe Qiang risings bled the west for twenty years, burned 3.2 billion on campaigns, emptied the exchequer, and dragged inland provinces into want.

sentences.zh: 沖質短祚，桓靈不軌。

translations.literal: The emperors Chong and Zhi enjoyed only brief fates; Huan and Ling deviated from the proper track.
translations.idiomatic: Infant emperors Chong and Zhi died young; Huan and Ling turned criminal.

sentences.zh: ，南宮災，延及北闕。

translations.literal: The Southern Palace caught fire, and the blaze reached the northern gate-towers.
translations.idiomatic: Flames swept the Southern Palace up to the northern watch-towers.

sentences.zh: 於是復收天下田畝十錢，用營宮宇。

translations.literal: Thereupon they again collected ten cash per mu of field throughout the realm to fund palace construction.
translations.idiomatic: The court reimposed a ten-cash-per-mu surcharge empire-wide to pay for new halls.

sentences.zh: 帝出自侯門，居貧即位，常曰：「桓帝不能作家，曾無私蓄。

translations.literal: The emperor came from a marquis household, had grown up in poverty when he took the throne, and often said: 'Emperor Huan could not manage a household—he never built private savings.'
translations.idiomatic: Raised a poor cousin from a marquis line, Ling complained that Huan died without a secret hoard.

sentences.zh: 」故于西園造萬金堂，以為私藏。

translations.literal: Therefore he built the Hall of Myriad Gold in the Western Garden to serve as his private treasury.
translations.idiomatic: So he stacked West Garden's Ten Thousand Jin Hall as a personal strongbox.

sentences.zh: 復寄小黃門私錢，家至巨億。

translations.literal: He also deposited cash with junior palace attendants until his household wealth reached hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: He parked fortunes with junior eunuchs until private sums hit astronomical figures.

sentences.zh: 於是懸鴻都之牓，開賣官之路，公卿以降，悉有等差。

translations.literal: Thereupon they posted notices at Hongdu Gate and opened the sale of offices; from public ministers downward every grade had its price.
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu notices priced every title from minister on down.

sentences.zh: 廷尉崔烈入錢五百萬以買司徒，刺史二千石遷除，皆責助治宮室錢，大郡至二千萬錢，不畢者或至自殺。

translations.literal: Court Commandant Cui Lie paid five million cash to buy the post of minister of education; when prefects and two-thousand-bushel officials were promoted or transferred, each had to contribute toward palace repairs—great commanderies owed up to twenty million cash, and some who could not finish paying killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lie bought the ministry of education for five million; moving a prefect meant a repair levy—two thousand strings for the richest circuits—and failure drove men to suicide.

sentences.zh: 獻帝作五銖錢，而有四道連於邊緣。

translations.literal: Emperor Xian minted wushu coins, but four raised ridges ran along their rims.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's five-zhu pieces bore four ridges along the edge.

sentences.zh: 有識者尤之曰：「豈京師破壞，此錢四出也。」

translations.literal: Men of insight blamed them, saying: 'Surely the capital is demolished—this cash is fleeing in four directions.'
translations.idiomatic: Critics called it an omen: a ruined capital with coin scattering to the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 及董卓尋戈，火焚宮室，乃劫鸞駕，西幸長安，悉壞五銖錢，更鑄小錢，盡收長安及洛陽銅人飛廉之屬，以充鼓鑄。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo brandished his spear, torched the palace compounds, hijacked the imperial carriage, and fled west to Chang'an, he destroyed all wushu coinage, recast inferior small cash, and melted down every bronze man and Flying-Lian statue in Chang'an and Luoyang to supply the mints.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's coup fired the palaces, dragged the court to Chang'an, voided five-zhu currency for light little coins, and fed the furnaces with Luoyang's bronze giants.

sentences.zh: 又錢無輪郭，文章不便。

translations.literal: Moreover the coins lacked rims and raised bands; their inscriptions were hard to use.
translations.idiomatic: The new issue had no inner ring and carried clumsy legends.

sentences.zh: 時人以為秦始皇見長人于臨洮，乃鑄銅人。

translations.literal: People of the time thought that when the First Emperor of Qin saw a giant at Lintao he cast the bronze giants.
translations.idiomatic: Wits linked the deed to Qin Shihuang casting the twelve giants after the Lintao giant tale.

sentences.zh: 卓，臨洮人也，興毀不同，凶訛相類。

translations.literal: Zhuo was a man of Lintao; destruction and creation differed, yet the sinister omens matched.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo hailed from Lintao—different outcomes, same dark rhyme.

sentences.zh: 及卓誅死，李傕、郭汜自相攻伐，于長安城中以為戰地。

translations.literal: After Zhuo was killed, Li Jue and Guo Si attacked one another and turned the city of Chang'an into a battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: Once Dong Zhuo fell, Li Jue and Guo Si turned Chang'an streets into war lanes.

sentences.zh: 是時穀一斛五十萬，豆麥二十萬，人相食啖，白骨盈積，殘骸餘肉，臭穢道路。

translations.literal: At that time one hu of grain cost five hundred thousand cash; beans and wheat two hundred thousand; people ate one another; white bones piled up; leftover flesh and mangled bodies fouled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Grain hit half a million cash the hu, beans two hundred thousand; cannibalism returned, bones heaped, gore slick on the pavement.

sentences.zh: 帝使侍御史侯汶出太倉米豆，為饑民作糜，經日頒佈而死者愈多。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Supervising Secretary Hou Wen to issue grain and beans from the great granary and cook gruel for the starving; distributions ran day after day yet the dead multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent Hou Wen to ladle imperial stores into gruel kettles, but daily handouts only raised the death toll.

sentences.zh: 帝於是始疑有司盜其糧廩，乃親於御前自加臨給，饑者人皆泣曰：「今始得耳！

translations.literal: The emperor therefore began to suspect his clerks of embezzling the granaries; he personally supervised distribution before the imperial lectern, whereupon the starving all wept, 'Only now do we truly receive it!'
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting theft, the emperor ladled porridge himself—starvelings sobbed that they were eating for the first time.

sentences.zh: 」帝東歸也，李傕、郭汜等追敗乘輿于曹陽，夜潛渡河，六宮皆步。

translations.literal: When the emperor marched east, Li Jue, Guo Si, and others pursued and defeated the imperial train at Caoyang; at night he forded the river in secret, and the entire six palaces went on foot.
translations.idiomatic: On the eastward trek Li and Guo smashed the cavalcade at Caoyang; the court forded the river by night on foot, ladies-in-waiting and all.

sentences.zh: 初出營欄，後手持縑數匹，董承使符節令孫徽以刃脅奪之，殺旁侍者，血濺後服。

translations.literal: They first fled the stockade camp; afterward the empress carried several bolts of silk; Director of Insignia Sun Hui, acting on Dong Cheng's orders, threatened her with a blade to seize them and killed attendants beside her; blood splashed the empress's robe.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing the palisade, the empress hugged silk bolts until Sun Hui, under Dong Cheng's orders, pressed a blade to her throat, slaughtered her maids, and splashed her gown.

sentences.zh: 既至安邑，御衣穿敗，唯以野棗園菜以為餱糧。

translations.literal: Once they reached Anyi, the imperial wardrobe was in tatters; they relied solely on wild jujubes and garden vegetables for dry rations.
translations.idiomatic: At Anyi the imperial wardrobe was shreds; the court lived on foraged jujubes and greens.

sentences.zh: 自此長安城中盡空，並皆四散，二三年間，關中無復行人。

translations.literal: From then on Chang'an stood empty within its walls; everyone scattered; within two or three years not a traveler crossed Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an emptied; within seasons Guanzhong saw no travellers.

sentences.zh: 建安元年，車駕至洛陽，宮闈蕩滌，百官披荊棘而居焉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jian'an the imperial carriage reached Luoyang; palace chambers had been swept bare, and the hundred officials dwelt among brambles.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an year one brought the court to a Luoyang scraped bare—ministers camped in thorns.

sentences.zh: 州郡各擁強兵，而委輸不至，尚書郎官自出采穭，或不能自反，死於墟巷。

translations.literal: Each province and commandery clutched strong armies, but tribute ceased to arrive; secretaries and gentlemen of the ministries went out themselves to cut hay; some never returned and died in ruined lanes.
translations.idiomatic: Warlords hoarded arms while revenue stopped; clerks scythed their own fodder and died in alleys.

sentences.zh: 魏武之初，九州雲擾，攻城掠地，保此懷民，軍旅之資，權時調給。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wu of Wei the nine provinces were in turmoil; he besieged cities and seized territory while sheltering the people who surrendered; military supplies were met by temporary levies as circumstances allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's early years besieged towns, annexed land, and fed friendlies on ad hoc impressment.

sentences.zh: 于時袁紹軍人皆資椹棗，袁術戰士取給蠃蒲。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Shao's troops relied on oak flour and jujubes; Yuan Shu's soldiers drew mulberries and clams and pondweed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao's army ate milled oak and dates; Yuan Shu's ranks scraped mussels, snails, and pondweed.

sentences.zh: 魏武於是乃募良民屯田許下，又於州郡列置田官，歲有數千萬斛，以充兵戎之用。

translations.literal: Thereupon Emperor Wu of Wei recruited commoners for agricultural colonies at Xu and furthermore set field officers in each province and commandery; every year they harvested tens of millions of hu to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then colonized peasants around Xu, planted intendants in every province, and pulled tens of millions of hu yearly for the hosts.

sentences.zh: 及初平袁氏，以定鄴都，令收田租畝粟四升，戶絹二匹而綿二斤，餘皆不得擅興，藏強賦弱。

translations.literal: When he had first pacified the Yuans and secured Ye, he ordered land rent collected at four sheng of millet per mu, two bolts of tabby per household plus two jin of floss; nothing else might be imposed without authorization, lest powerful households hoard and weak ones suffer.
translations.idiomatic: After beating the Yuans and holding Ye he capped rent at four sheng per mu and two bolts plus two jin of silk per door—no other impost without leave, guarding smallholders from powerful estates.

sentences.zh: 文帝黃初二年，以穀貴，始罷五銖錢。

translations.literal: In the second Huangchu year of Emperor Wen of Wei, because grain was dear, he first abolished wushu coin.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu 2 ended five-zhu coinage when millet spiked.

sentences.zh: 于時天下未並，戎車歲動，孔子曰，「加之以師旅，因之以饑饉」，此言兵凶之謀而沴氣應之也。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was not yet unified; war wagons moved every year; Confucius says, 'Add armies to it, add famine upon famine'—this speaks of the scheming of military calamity and the responding ill-omened vapors.
translations.idiomatic: With the realm still split and campaigns annual, Confucius's warning—armies stacked on dearth—matched the miasma of civil war.

sentences.zh: 于時三方之人，志相吞滅，戰勝攻取，耕夫釋耒，江淮之鄉，尤缺儲峙。

translations.literal: At that time the three sides intended to swallow one another; victory and conquest followed one upon another; ploughmen dropped their ploughs; along the Yangzi and Huai especially, reserves ran short.
translations.idiomatic: The three kingdoms gnawed at each other; farmers dropped implements; the Huai-Yangzi belt ran dry of stores.

sentences.zh: 吳上大將軍陸遜抗疏，請令諸將各廣其田。

translations.literal: Grand General Lu Xun of Wu submitted a memorial asking each commander to expand his farm plots.
translations.idiomatic: Wu grand general Lu Xun begged every general to enlarge military farms.

sentences.zh: 權報曰：「甚善。

translations.literal: Sun Quan replied: 'Excellent.'
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan answered: 'Very good.'

sentences.zh: 今孤父子親自受田，車中八牛，以為四耦。

translations.literal: Now I and my sons personally take the plough; eight oxen stand in the cart, forming four pairs.
translations.idiomatic: From now my heir and I drive the plough ourselves—eight oxen hitched as four yokes.

sentences.zh: 雖未及古人，亦欲與眾均其勞也。

translations.literal: Although we have not reached the ancients, we still wish to share the labor with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: We fall short of ancient models, yet we mean to sweat beside the ranks.

sentences.zh: 」有吳之務農重穀，始於此焉。

translations.literal: Within Wu the earnest attention to farming and grain began from this.
translations.idiomatic: That marked Wu's turn toward serious tillage.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝不恭，淫于宮籞，百僚編於手役，天下失其躬稼。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei lacked reverence and indulged the inner harem; the hundred officials were bound to menial labor, and the realm lost its personal farming.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mingdi chased palace pleasures, impressed ministers as laborers, and let agriculture slip.

sentences.zh: 此後關東遇水，民亡產業，而興師遼陽，坐甲江甸，皆以國乏經用，胡可勝言。

translations.literal: Afterward Guandong suffered floods and the people lost their estates, yet armies marched on Liaodong and armor sat along the Yangzi—all because the state lacked routine revenue; how can one tell it all?
translations.idiomatic: Later floods ruined Guandong homes while expeditions struck Liaodong and fleets massed on the Yangzi—short treasury, endless grief.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝，既平孫皓，納百萬而罄三吳之資，接千年而總西蜀之用，韜干戈於府庫，破舟船于江壑，河濱海岸，三丘八藪，耒耨之所不至者，人皆受焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu the Founder, having subdued Sun Hao, absorbed a million households and emptied the resources of the three Wu commanderies; linking a thousand years of inheritance he gathered the wealth of western Shu; he sheathed weapons in the arsenals and smashed boats in the river gorges; along riverbanks and sea strands, every hillock and marsh—wherever the plough had not reached—people received land.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sun Hao surrendered, Jin swallowed million-household Wu, tapped Shu hoards, stacked arms in magazines, broke river fleets, and parcelled waste acres to settlers.

sentences.zh: 農祥晨正，平秩東作，荷鍤贏糧，有同雲布。

translations.literal: The auspicious star for farming stood at dawn due east; they ranked and supervised eastern tillage; men shouldered hoes and bore grain like clouds spreading.
translations.idiomatic: With the agrarian asterism at dawn they ordered eastern fields; labourers shouldered hoes and grain like clouds rolling out.

sentences.zh: 若夫因天而資五緯，因地而興五材，世屬升平，物流倉府，宮闈增飾，服玩相輝。

translations.literal: If they relied on heaven to deploy the five planetary emblems and on earth to raise the five materials, ages marked uninterrupted peace, goods flowed and granaries filled, inner chambers grew ever finer, and garments and playthings outshone one another.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's five planets and earth's five stuffs aligned; peace filled treasuries; palace dress and toys sparkled in rivalry.

sentences.zh: 於是王君夫、武子、石崇等更相誇尚，輿服鼎俎之盛，連衡帝室，布金埒之泉，粉珊瑚之樹，物盛則衰，固其宜也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Jun, Shi Chong, and others vied in extravagance; the splendor of carriages, robes, cauldrons, and stands rivaled the imperial house; they spread coin like a golden embankment and powdered coral trees; when things flourish to excess, decline is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun and Shi Chong outspent one another—carriages, robes, and bronze rivaling the throne, coin heaped like berms, coral dusted like trees—luxury sowing its own fall.

sentences.zh: 永甯之初，洛中尚有錦帛四百萬，珠寶金銀百餘斛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongning, Luoyang still held four million bolts of brocade and tabby and over a hundred hu of pearls, gems, gold, and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Early Yongning Luoyang still hoarded four million bolts of silk and a hundred hu of bullion and pearl.

sentences.zh: 惠後北征，蕩陰反駕，寒桃在禦，只雞以給，其布衾兩幅，囊錢三千，以為車駕之資焉。

translations.literal: When Empress Hui marched north, her carriage turned back at Dangyin; cold peaches were all the imperial table held; a single chicken supplied meat; her bedding was two plain cloths; three thousand cash in a purse—such was the treasury for the imperial train.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's northern march stalled at Dangyin on cold peaches, one chicken, two cotton quilts, and three thousand cash for the whole cortège.

sentences.zh: 懷帝為劉曜所圍，王師累敗，府帑既竭，百官饑甚，比屋不見火煙，饑人自相啖食。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai, besieged by Liu Yao, saw imperial armies defeated again and again; the treasury was exhausted; officials starved miserably; house after house showed no cooking smoke; the starving ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged by Liu Yao, Huai watched armies shatter, stores vanish, ministers starve, hearths go cold, and survivors turn cannibal.

sentences.zh: 湣皇西宅，餒饉弘多，斗米二金，死者太半。

translations.literal: Emperor Min dwelt in the west; famine ran deepest; one dou of rice cost two jin of gold and more than half the people perished.
translations.idiomatic: Min's western court faced famine so brutal that two ounces of gold bought one dou of rice and half the population died.

sentences.zh: 劉曜陳兵，內外斷絕，十之曲，屑而供帝，君臣相顧，莫不揮涕。

translations.literal: Liu Yao deployed his troops; internal and external communication was cut off; grain measures were reduced to crumbs that they ground to supply the emperor; ruler and ministers looked at one another; none failed to shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao sealed the city; when only scrapings from the grain jars could be ground for the sovereign, throne and ministers met each other's eyes weeping.

sentences.zh: 元後渡江，軍事草創，蠻陬賧布，不有恆准，中府所儲，數四千匹。

translations.literal: After Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi, military affairs were still in embryo; tribute cloth from southern tribes had no fixed standard; what the central treasury stored amounted to only several thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's southern crossing left armies half-built; barbarian cloth tribute lacked a steady gauge; central stores held a mere few thousand bolts.

sentences.zh: 于時石勒勇銳，挻亂淮南，帝懼其侵逼，甚患之，乃詔方鎮云，有斬石勒首者，賞布千匹云。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Le was fierce and thrust turmoil into the Huai region; the emperor feared invasion and worried greatly, so he issued an edict to the regional commanders that whoever beheaded Shi Le would receive a reward of one thousand bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: With Shi Le hammering Huainan, the court offered a thousand bolts for his head to frontier generals.

sentences.zh: 漢自董卓之亂，百姓流離，穀石至五十餘萬，人多相食。

translations.literal: From the turmoil under Dong Zhuo in Han onward, common people drifted destitute; grain reached more than five hundred thousand cash per shi and many ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: After Dong Zhuo's coup, refugees wandered, grain hit five hundred thousand per shi, and cannibalism spread.

sentences.zh: 魏武既破黃巾，欲經略四方，而苦軍食不足，羽林監潁川棗祗建置屯田議。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu of Wei crushed the Yellow Turbans and wished to plan campaigns in every direction, he suffered shortage of army grain; the paladin supervisor Zao Zhi of Yingchuan proposed establishing agricultural colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Planning wider wars after the Turbans, Cao Cao lacked rations until Yingchuan's Zao Zhi urged military farms.

sentences.zh: 魏武乃令曰：「夫定國之術在於強兵足食，秦人以急農兼天下，孝武以屯田定西域，此先世之良式也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei then ordered: 'The art of stabilizing the state lies in strong armies and full bellies. The men of Qin unified the realm through urgent farming; Emperor Wu of Han secured the Western Regions through garrison fields—these are excellent precedents from antiquity.'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao decreed that power rests on soldiers and full granaries—citing Qin's agrarian drive and Han's frontier colonies.

sentences.zh: 」於是以任峻為典農中郎將，募百姓屯田許下，得穀百萬斛。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed Ren Jun as attendant-at-camps colonel of agriculture, recruited commoners to colonize land around Xu, and harvested a million hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He named Ren Jun colonel of agriculture, settled peasants around Xu, and reaped a million hu.

sentences.zh: 郡國列置田官，數年之中，所在積粟，倉廩皆滿。

translations.literal: Commanderies and kingdoms established field officers; within a few years grain piled up wherever they were and every granary stood full.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces posted farm directors; within years bins brimmed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 祗死，魏武后追思其功，封爵其子。

translations.literal: When Zao Zhi died, Emperor Wu of Wei later remembered his achievement and enfeoffed his son.
translations.idiomatic: After Zao Zhi died, Cao Cao ennobled his son in remembrance.

sentences.zh: 建安初，關中百姓流入荊州者十餘萬家，及聞本土安寧，皆企望思歸，而無以自業。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jian'an more than a hundred thousand households of Guanzhong commoners had flowed into Jingzhou; when they heard their homeland was peaceful they longed to return but possessed no means of livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jian'an saw a hundred thousand Guanzhong households flee to Jing; peace at home made them ache to go back, yet they had no tools to farm.

sentences.zh: 於是衛覬議為「鹽者國之大寶，自喪亂以來放散，今宜如舊置使者監賣，以其直益市犁牛，百姓歸者以供給之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wei Ji argued that 'Salt is the state's great treasure; since the turmoil it has been scattered; now we should as of old appoint agents to supervise sales, use the proceeds to buy plough oxen, and supply those who return.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ji argued salt was the dynastic treasure—restore government sales, spend proceeds on oxen, and equip returning refugees.

sentences.zh: 勤耕積粟，以豐殖關中，遠者聞之，必多競還。

translations.literal: 'Urge plowing and pile grain to enrich Guanzhong; those far away who hear of it will surely race to come home.'
translations.idiomatic: Fatten Guanzhong with tillage and wanderers will sprint homeward.

sentences.zh: 」於是魏武遣謁者僕射監鹽官，移司隸校尉居弘農。

translations.literal: Thereupon Emperor Wu of Wei dispatched the herald chief superintendent to oversee salt offices and moved the metropolitan inspector to Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent the herald's vice to watch salt monopolies and shifted the provincial inspector to Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 流人果還，關中豐實。

translations.literal: The wanderers indeed returned; Guanzhong grew ample.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees indeed streamed back; Guanzhong filled out.

sentences.zh: 既而又以沛國劉馥為揚州刺史，鎮合肥，廣屯田，修芍陂、茹陂、七門、吳塘諸堨，以溉稻田，公私有蓄，歷代為利。

translations.literal: Later he also appointed Liu Fu of Pei as inspector of Yangzhou, stationed at Hefei, broadly opened agricultural colonies, and repaired the weirs at Quebei, Rubi, Qimen, and Wutang to irrigate rice paddies, so that public and private stores accumulated and posterity profited for generations.
translations.idiomatic: He then posted Liu Fu at Hefei to expand garrison farms, rebuild Quebei, Rubi, Qimen, and Wutang dikes for rice, filling public and private granaries for generations.

sentences.zh: 賈逵之為豫州，南與吳接，修守戰之具，堨汝水，造新陂，又通運渠二百餘里，所謂賈侯渠者也。

translations.literal: When Jia Kua held Yuzhou, bordering Wu to the south, he repaired gear for defense and assault, dammed the Ru River to build new ponds, and opened a transport canal over two hundred li long—the so-called Marquis Jia Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kua, guarding Yu against Wu, readied arms, dammed the Ru into new reservoirs, and cut the two-hundred-li Jia Hou canal for supply.

sentences.zh: 當黃初中，四方郡守懇田又加，以故國用不匱。

translations.literal: During the Huangchu years, reclamation by governors of the four quarters increased further, so state expenditure never ran short.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huangchu, county reclamation kept spreading, and the treasury stayed solvent.

sentences.zh: 時濟北顏斐為京兆太守，京兆自馬超之亂，百姓不專農殖，乃無車牛。

translations.literal: At that time Yan Fei of Jibei served as governor of Jingzhao; since the turmoil of Ma Chao the people had not devoted themselves to farming, and they lacked carts and oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Fei of Jibei governed Jingzhao after Ma Chao's rising had pulled farmers from the plough—there were no draft animals left.

sentences.zh: 斐又課百姓，令閑月取車材，轉相教匠。

translations.literal: Fei also assigned the common people, ordering them in slack months to gather cart timber and pass it along to train carpenters.
translations.idiomatic: He levied farmers to stockpile wheelwrights' lumber in off-seasons and rotated apprenticeships among smiths.

sentences.zh: 其無牛者令養豬，投貴賣以買牛。

translations.literal: Those without oxen he ordered to raise pigs, sell them when prices were high, and buy oxen with the proceeds.
translations.idiomatic: Households short an ox were told to fatten hogs, sell into a dear market, and trade up to cattle.

sentences.zh: 始者皆以為煩，一二年中編戶皆有車牛，于田役省贍，京兆遂以豐沃。

translations.literal: At first everyone thought it burdensome, but within a year or two every registered household had carts and oxen; field labor and corvée cost half as much in upkeep, and Jingzhao turned fertile and rich.
translations.idiomatic: Grumbling gave way within two seasons to ox-drawn carts county-wide, lighter field service, and a flush Jingzhao plain.

sentences.zh: 鄭渾為沛郡太守，郡居下濕，水澇為患，百姓饑乏。

translations.literal: Zheng Hun became governor of Pei commandery; the seat lay low and damp, inundation was chronic, and the people were hungry and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Pei's capital sat on soggy ground—floods and famine followed Zheng Hun's appointment.

sentences.zh: 渾于蕭、相二縣興陂堨，開稻田，郡人皆不以為便。

translations.literal: Hun raised weirs in Xiao and Xiang counties, opening paddy fields; the people of the commandery all deemed it inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: He diked the Xiao–Xiang marshes for rice land while locals complained about the disruption.

sentences.zh: 渾以為終有經久之利，遂躬率百姓興功，一冬皆成。

translations.literal: Hun believed there would in the end be lasting profit, so he personally led the people in the project, and in one winter it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Hun overruled them, worked beside the crews, and finished every dike that winter.

sentences.zh: 比年大收，頃畝歲增，租入倍常，郡中賴其利，刻石頌之，號曰鄭陂。

translations.literal: Year after year the harvest was abundant; yields per qing rose annually, and rent revenue doubled the usual; the commandery relied on the benefit, carved an inscription praising him, and named it the Zheng Weir.
translations.idiomatic: Record crops followed; rents doubled the norm, so the county cut a stele to the 'Zheng dike' that still fed them.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝世徐邈為涼州，土地少雨，常苦乏穀。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Ming of Wei, Xu Miao governed Liang Province; the land received little rain and always suffered grain shortages.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mingdi sent Xu Miao to Liangzhou, where drought chronically starved the granaries.

sentences.zh: 邈上修武威、酒泉鹽池，以收虜穀。

translations.literal: Miao memorialized to repair the salt lakes of Wuwei and Jiuquan, using the income to purchase tribal grain.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the Wuwei and Jiuquan salt pans and spent the proceeds buying grain from the border peoples.

sentences.zh: 又廣開水田，募貧民佃之，家家豐足，倉庫盈溢。

translations.literal: He also widely opened irrigated paddies, recruited poor tenants, so that every household was well supplied and granaries overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Wet-field reclamation and poor tenants followed until bins spilled over.

sentences.zh: 及度支州界軍用之餘，以市金錦犬馬，通供中國之費，西域人入貢，財貨流通，皆邈之功也。

translations.literal: When funds beyond the provincial army budget remained, he used them to buy gold, brocade, dogs, and horses for central court expenses; western-region envoys brought tribute and goods circulated—all Xu Miao's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus salt revenue bought luxuries for Luoyang and kept frontier trade alive—credit Xu Miao.

sentences.zh: 其後皇甫隆為敦煌太守，敦煌俗不作耬犁，及不知用水，人牛功力既費，而收穀更少。

translations.literal: Later, when Huangfu Long became governor of Dunhuang, local custom did not employ drill-seeders or understand irrigation; labor from men and oxen was wasted while harvests shrank.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Long found Dunhuang still scratching drills without irrigation—costly effort, meager grain.

sentences.zh: 隆到，乃教作耬犁，又教使灌溉。

translations.literal: When Long arrived, he taught them to build drill-seeders and also taught irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: He introduced seed drills and channel watering.

sentences.zh: 歲終率計，所省庸力過半，得穀加五，西方以豐。

translations.literal: At year's end, when accounts were reckoned, hired labor was reduced by more than half and grain yields increased dramatically; the west thereby prospered.
translations.idiomatic: Year-end tallies showed payroll halved and yields multiplied—the northwest fattened.

sentences.zh: ，關中饑，宣帝表徙冀州農夫五千人佃上邽，興京兆、天水、南安鹽池，以益軍實。

translations.literal: When Guanzhong suffered famine, Emperor Xuan memorialized to move five thousand farmers from Ji Province to colonize Shanggui and to develop the salt pools of Jingzhao, Tianshui, and Nan'an in order to enlarge military stores.
translations.idiomatic: A Guanzhong drought drew Sima Yi's memorial: shift five thousand Ji farmers to Shanggui and work the Jingzhao–Tianshui–Nan'an brine pans for army grain.

sentences.zh: ，開成國渠自陳倉至槐里；

translations.literal: They opened the Chengguo Canal from Chencang to Huaili;
translations.idiomatic: They cut the Chengguo Canal between Chencang and Huaili.

sentences.zh: 築臨晉陂，引汧洛溉舄鹵之地三千餘頃，國以充實焉。

translations.literal: they built the Linjin weir, drew the Qian and Luo to irrigate more than three thousand qing of alkaline soil, and the state grew ample thereby.
translations.idiomatic: The Linjin barrage steered the Qian and Luo onto thirty thousand acres of salty flats until the exchequer filled.

sentences.zh: ，宣帝又督諸軍伐吳將諸葛恪，焚其積聚，恪棄城遁走。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan again supervised the various armies in attacking Wu general Zhuge Ke, burned Ke's stockpiled grain, and Ke abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi next led the strike on Zhuge Ke—torched Wu supplies and drove Ke from his walls.

sentences.zh: 帝因欲廣田積穀，為兼併之計，乃使鄧艾行陳、項以東，至壽春地。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore wished to broaden fields and pile grain for a strategy of piecemeal annexation, and sent Deng Ai to survey east from Chen and Xiang as far as the Shouchun region.
translations.idiomatic: Intent on annexing Huainan inch by inch, the court dispatched Deng Ai to scout from Chen–Xiang toward Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 艾以為田良水少，不足以盡地利，宜開河渠，可以大積軍糧，又通運漕之道。

translations.literal: Ai held that the soil was good but water scarce—not enough to exhaust the land's potential—and that rivers and canals should be opened to stockpile army grain in quantity and also link transport routes.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai reported rich soil but unreliable rain; canals could flood the granaries and float supplies.

sentences.zh: 乃著《濟河論》以喻其指。

translations.literal: He therefore composed the 'Treatise on the Ji River' to explain his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He framed the argument in his 'Discourse on Channeling the Ji.'

sentences.zh: 又以為昔破黃巾，因為屯田，積穀許都，以制四方。

translations.literal: He also argued that when the Yellow Turbans were crushed in former times, agricultural colonies had been founded and grain piled at Xu so as to control the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He reminded them how colony farms around Xu had fed the defeat of the Turbans.

sentences.zh: 今三隅已定，事在淮南。

translations.literal: Now the three corners were settled; what remained lay in Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: With three fronts quiet, only Huainan still mattered.

sentences.zh: 每大軍征舉，運兵過半，功費巨億，以為大役。

translations.literal: Whenever great armies mobilized, more than half the burden was moving troops—costs ran to hundreds of millions and constituted a vast undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Each campaign burned logistics—half the effort was convoys—and bills ran into billions of cash.

sentences.zh: 陳蔡之間，土下田良，可省許昌左右諸稻田，並水東下。

translations.literal: Between Chen and Cai the ground was low and fertile; one could retire the paddy fields around Xuchang and send all the water eastward.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen–Cai depression could soak up irrigation shed from the Xuchang rice plots if sluices turned east.

sentences.zh: 令淮北二萬人、淮南三萬人分休，且佃且守。

translations.literal: Order twenty thousand men north of the Huai and thirty thousand south of it to rotate rest with farming and guarding.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed fifty thousand men alternating guard duty with tillage on both banks of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 水豐，常收三倍于西，計除眾費，歲完五百萬斛以為軍資。

translations.literal: With abundant water, harvests constantly tripled those west of the river; deducting all expenses, five million hu could be delivered yearly for military supply.
translations.idiomatic: Wet years tripled western yields; after costs, five million hu a year could arm the campaigns.

sentences.zh: 六七年間，可積三千萬餘斛於淮北，此則十萬之眾五年食也。

translations.literal: In six or seven years one could stockpile over thirty million hu north of the Huai—food enough for an army of one hundred thousand for five years.
translations.idiomatic: Six or seven harvests could stack thirty million hu north of the river—five years' rations for a hundred-thousand-man host.

sentences.zh: 以此乘敵，無不克矣。

translations.literal: With this to strike the enemy, nothing would withstand you.
translations.idiomatic: Such reserves would break any southern defense.

sentences.zh: 宣帝善之，皆如艾計施行。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan approved it and implemented everything according to Ai's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi signed off and executed Deng Ai's blueprint.

sentences.zh: 遂北臨淮水，自鐘離而南橫石以西，盡沘水四百餘里，五里置一營，營六十人，且佃且守。

translations.literal: They therefore pressed north to the Huai River; from Zhongli south to west of Hengshi, and along the Bi River for over four hundred li, every five li they placed a camp of sixty men who farmed while they guarded.
translations.idiomatic: They lined the Huai from Zhongli past Hengshi—four hundred li of Bi River front—posting sixty-man camps every five li to plough under arms.

sentences.zh: 兼修廣淮陽、百尺二渠，上引河流，下通淮潁，大治諸陂于潁南、潁北，穿渠三百餘里，溉田二萬頃，淮南、淮北皆相連接。

translations.literal: They also widened the Huaiyang and Baichi canals, drawing the great river above and linking Huai and Ying below, greatly repairing the various weirs south and north of the Ying, cutting channels over three hundred li and irrigating twenty thousand qing of fields; Huainan and north of the Huai linked into one network.
translations.idiomatic: They dredged Huaiyang and Baichi, tied the Yellow River spill to Huai and Ying, refaced north–south Ying dikes, bored three hundred li of trench, and knitted Huai south and north across twenty thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 自壽春到京師，農官兵田，雞犬之聲，阡陌相屬。

translations.literal: From Shouchun to the capital, military colonies lined the fields; the crowing of chickens and barking of dogs rose along paths that stretched unbroken.
translations.idiomatic: Between Shouchun and Luoyang, garrison farms crowded the roads—chickens and dogs crowding the same dikes.

sentences.zh: 每東南有事，大軍出征，泛舟而下，達于江淮，資食有儲，而無水害，艾所建也。

translations.literal: Whenever trouble arose in the southeast and great armies marched out, boats floated downstream to reach the Yangzi and Huai; provisions lay stored and flood harm was avoided—this was what Ai built.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever southeast campaigns launched, barges slid down safe channels to the Yangzi–Huai junction with grain to spare—Deng Ai's hydraulic shield.

sentences.zh: 及晉受命，武帝欲平一江表。

translations.literal: When Jin received the mandate, Emperor Wu wished to pacify the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei–Jin transition, Emperor Wu set his sights on south of the Great River.

sentences.zh: 時穀賤而布帛貴，帝欲立平糴法，用布帛市穀，以為糧儲。

translations.literal: At that time grain was cheap while cloth and silk were dear; the emperor wished to establish equitable-purchase regulations, using cloth and silk to buy grain for reserves.
translations.idiomatic: Cheap grain and dear silk tempted him to institute pingdi purchases—swap bolts for bushels.

sentences.zh: 議者謂軍資尚少，不宜以貴易賤。

translations.literal: Discussants said military supplies were still insufficient and it was unsuitable to trade the expensive for the cheap.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers balked: armies still hungry, bad time to trade pricey silk for cheap grain.

sentences.zh: ，帝乃下詔曰：「夫百姓年豐則用奢，凶荒則窮匱，是相報之理也。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore issued an edict: 'When common people have bumper years they spend extravagantly; in famine years they are utterly destitute—such is the way they answer one another.'
translations.idiomatic: So Wu Di explained his logic: plenty breeds waste, dearth breeds ruin—a seasonal swing.

sentences.zh: 故古人權量國用，取贏散滯，有輕重平糴之法。

translations.literal: 'Hence the ancients weighed state expenditure, skimmed surplus and dispersed stagnation, and applied light-and-heavy equitable-purchase methods.'
translations.idiomatic: Ancient treasuries stabilized prices by buying cheap surpluses and selling stores when grain spiked.

sentences.zh: 理財鈞施，惠而不費，政之善者也。

translations.literal: 'To regulate wealth evenly and bestow blessing without waste is the excellence of government.'
translations.idiomatic: Balanced fiscal relief without waste—that was sage administration.

sentences.zh: 然此事廢久，天下希習其宜。

translations.literal: 'Yet this practice has long lapsed, and the realm rarely grows accustomed to its proper use.'
translations.idiomatic: But pingdi had lain dormant so long that officials no longer knew the drill.

sentences.zh: 加以官蓄未廣，言者異同，財貨未能達通其制。

translations.literal: 'Moreover official reserves are not yet broad; speakers disagree; goods and currency cannot yet circulate under the system.'
translations.idiomatic: State bins were still thin, debate gridlocked, and coin could not yet move through the scheme.

sentences.zh: 更令國寶散於穰歲而上不收，貧弱困于荒年而國無備。

translations.literal: 'It further lets the state's treasure scatter in fat years while it fails to collect above, and leaves the poor and weak trapped in bad years while the state has no stores.'
translations.idiomatic: Fat years still leaked bullion upward while lean years trapped peasants with empty granaries.

sentences.zh: 豪人富商，挾輕資，蘊重積，以管其利。

translations.literal: 'Magnates and great merchants hoard light capital and pile heavy stores to monopolize the profit.'
translations.idiomatic: Magnates parked liquid silver and cornered hoards.

sentences.zh: 故農夫苦其業，而末作不可禁也。

translations.literal: 'Therefore farmers suffer at their work, while craft and trade cannot be forbidden.'
translations.idiomatic: Tillers bore the squeeze while artisan trades stayed unstoppable.

sentences.zh: 今者省徭務本，並力墾殖，欲令農功益登，耕者益勸，而猶或騰踴，至於農人並傷。

translations.literal: 'Now we have reduced corvée and urged the root [agriculture], joined strength in reclamation, wishing to make farming yield more abundantly and tillers more eager, yet prices still leap until farmers are doubly hurt.'
translations.idiomatic: Even after cutting labor dues and pushing reclamation, price spikes still doubled farmers' pain.

sentences.zh: 今宜通糴，以充儉乏。

translations.literal: 'Now we should open equitable purchase to supply want in lean years.'
translations.idiomatic: Pingdi purchases must bridge the next shortage.

sentences.zh: 主者平議，具為條制。

translations.literal: 'Let the responsible officials deliberate evenly and set out the regulations in full.'
translations.idiomatic: Ministers were told to draft executable statutes.

sentences.zh: 」然事竟未行。

translations.literal: 'Yet in the end the matter was not carried out.'
translations.idiomatic: Nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 是時江南未平，朝廷厲精於稼牆。

translations.literal: At that time the south of the Yangzi was not yet pacified; the court devoted intense effort to farming.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiangnan still hostile, Luoyang obsessed over every furrow.

sentences.zh: 四年正月丁亥，帝親耕藉田。

translations.literal: On the dinghai day of the first month of the fourth year, the emperor personally ploughed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai in Taishi year four he drove the sacred furrow himself.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，詔曰：「使四海之內，棄末反本，競農務功，能奉宣朕志，令百姓勸事樂業者，其唯郡縣長吏乎！

translations.literal: On gengyin he issued an edict: 'Within the four seas, to abandon secondary pursuits and return to the root, to compete in farming and labor—who but the magistrates of commanderies and counties can carry out my intent and make the hundred surnames diligent in their tasks and content in their livelihoods!'
translations.idiomatic: Two days later he demanded county magistrates turn every household back to the soil.

sentences.zh: 先之勞之，在於不倦。

translations.literal: 'To lead them and labor alongside them lies in tirelessness.'
translations.idiomatic: Leadership meant working beside subjects until exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 每念其經營職事，亦為勤矣。

translations.literal: 'Whenever I reflect that they manage their duties, I know they too are diligent.'
translations.idiomatic: He acknowledged their grind.

sentences.zh: 其以中左典牧種草馬，賜縣令長相及郡國丞各一匹。

translations.literal: 'Let grass-fed horses from the Central Left Herd Office be granted one head each to county magistrates, chiefs, and assistant governors of commanderies.'
translations.idiomatic: Grass-fed studs from the Central Left herd went one apiece to county and prefectural aides.

sentences.zh: 」是歲，乃立常平倉，豐則糴，儉則糶，以利百姓。

translations.literal: 'That same year the Ever-Normal Granary was established: in fat years it purchased; in lean years it sold—to benefit the common people.'
translations.idiomatic: That year saw the Ever-Normal Granary—buying dearths, selling gluts—for farmer relief.

sentences.zh: 五年正月癸巳，敕戒郡國計吏、諸郡國守相令長，務盡地利，禁游食商販。

translations.literal: On guisi day of the first month of the fifth year he admonished the provincial clerks and the governors and magistrates of every commandery and kingdom to exhaust land productivity and prohibit wandering eaters and peddlers.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi five opened with orders to maximize acreage and ban itinerant hawkers.

sentences.zh: 其休假者令與父兄同其勤勞，豪勢不得侵役寡弱，私相置名。

translations.literal: 'Those on leave shall share field labor with fathers and elders; powerful households must not press the weak into service or privately substitute names.'
translations.idiomatic: Leave-takers had to hoe beside kin; magnates could not draft proxies.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔以「司隸校尉石鑒所上汲郡太守王宏勤恤百姓，導化有方，督勸開荒五千餘頃，遇年普饑而郡界獨無匱乏，可謂能以勸教，時同功異者矣。

translations.literal: 'In the tenth month an edict declared: According to what Metropolitan Superintendent Shi Jian reported, Wang Hong, governor of Ji commandery, diligently cared for the common people and guided transformation with method; he supervised and urged the opening of more than five thousand qing of wasteland; when a general famine struck the year, only his commandery lacked shortage—truly one may say he could teach by encouragement and achieved a different merit in the same hour.'
translations.idiomatic: An autumn edict cited Shi Jian's report praising Ji prefect Wang Hong for opening five thousand qing while neighboring prefectures starved.

sentences.zh: 其賜穀千斛，佈告天下」。

translations.literal: 'Grant him one thousand hu of grain and proclaim this throughout the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: He earned a thousand-hu bonus and an empire-wide bulletin.

sentences.zh: 八年，司徒石苞奏：「州郡農桑未有殿最之制，宜增掾屬令史，有所循行。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Minister of Education Shi Bao memorialized: 'Commanderies and prefectures have no ranking system for farming and sericulture; subordinate clerks and scribes should be added so that there may be rounds of inspection.'
translations.idiomatic: In year eight Minister Shi Bao asked for farming inspectors under each prefect.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: 'The emperor approved.'
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 事見《石苞傳》。

translations.literal: The matter appears in the 'Biography of Shi Bao.'
translations.idiomatic: Details sit in Shi Bao's chapter.

sentences.zh: 苞既明於勸課，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Once Bao had clarified exhortation and inspection, the hundred surnames were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shi Bao tightened inspections, farmers steadied.

sentences.zh: 十年，光祿勳夏侯和上修新渠、富壽、游陂三渠，凡溉田千五百頃。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Minister of the Household Xia Houhe repaired the three canals Xinqu, Fushou, and Youpi—together irrigating fifteen hundred qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Year ten saw Xia Houhe rebuild Xinqu, Fushou, and Youpi—fifteen hundred qing wet.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔曰：「出戰入耕，雖自古之常，然事力未息，未嘗不以戰士為念也。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month an edict stated: 'Going out to battle and returning to plough—though this is the constant practice since antiquity, while military tasks have not ceased I have never failed to keep soldiers in mind.'
translations.idiomatic: A winter edict recalled soldiers even while praising the ancient plough-and-sword rhythm.

sentences.zh: 今以鄴奚官奴婢著新城，代田兵種稻，奴婢各五十人為一屯，屯置司馬，使皆如屯田法。

translations.literal: 'Now assign Ye's chamberlain slave girls and bondmaids to the new city to replace military colonists in planting rice; fifty slave girls form one tun, each tun having a marshal, all according to the agricultural colony regulations.'
translations.idiomatic: Ye palace bondwomen were moved to the new town to replace tun troops seeding rice—fifty women per tun under colony rules.

sentences.zh: 」三年，又詔曰：「今年霖雨過差，又有蟲災。

translations.literal: 'In the third year another edict said: This year unseasonal rains have been excessive and insect pests have also struck.'
translations.idiomatic: Third-year follow-up: freak rains and locusts.

sentences.zh: 潁川、襄城自春以來，略不下種，深以為慮。

translations.literal: 'From spring onward in Yingchuan and Xiangcheng sowing has barely occurred—I am deeply worried.'
translations.idiomatic: Yingchuan and Xiangcheng had barely seeded since spring.

sentences.zh: 主者何以為百姓計，促處當之。

translations.literal: 'How do responsible officials plan for the common people? Promptly settle appropriate measures.'
translations.idiomatic: Ministers had to answer how they would feed the people—fast.

sentences.zh: 」杜預上疏曰：

translations.literal: 'Du Yu submitted a memorial:'
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu answered with a memorial.

sentences.zh: 臣輒思惟，今者水災東南特劇，非但五稼不收，居業並損，下田所在停汙，高地皆多磽塉，此即百姓困窮方在來年。

translations.literal: 'Your servant has reflected that the present flooding in the southeast is especially severe; not only are the five grains failing to ripen, dwellings and livelihoods are ruined together; low fields lie drowned everywhere while high ground is mostly barren gravel—this means the people's distress will peak next year.'
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu warned that southeastern floods had drowned the crop and the cottage economy—mud flats and gravel ridges alike—and next year would hurt worse.

sentences.zh: 雖詔書切告長吏二千石為之設計，而不廓開大制，定其趣舍之宜，恐徒文具，所益蓋薄。

translations.literal: 'Although edicts urgently instruct prefects and two-thousand-bushel officials to devise plans, unless we open a large-scale system and fix what to adopt or abandon, I fear we shall only have empty documents and the benefit will be slight.'
translations.idiomatic: Without a sweeping plan, urgent edicts would stay ink on silk.

sentences.zh: 當今秋夏蔬食之時，而百姓已有不贍，前至冬春，野無青草，則必指仰官穀，以為生命。

translations.literal: 'It is now the season for autumn and summer vegetables, yet the people already lack enough; by the time we reach winter and spring, with no green grass in the wilds, they will certainly look only to official grain for their lives.'
translations.idiomatic: Vegetable season already left pantries bare; come winter they would depend wholly on state grain.

sentences.zh: 此乃一方之大事，不可不豫為思慮者也。

translations.literal: 'This is a great matter for the region and cannot fail to be planned in advance.'
translations.idiomatic: That demanded advance planning.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂既以水為困，當恃魚菜螺蜯，而洪波氾濫，貧弱者終不能得。

translations.literal: 'Your servant foolishly suggests that since we are trapped by water, we should rely on fish, vegetables, snails, and mussels; yet the flood spreads vast and the poor in the end cannot obtain them.'
translations.idiomatic: Fish and snails should help, but floods kept them from paupers.

sentences.zh: 今者宜大壞兗、豫州東界諸陂，隨其所歸而宣導之。

translations.literal: 'For now we ought greatly to breach the various weirs on the eastern border of Yan and Yu prefectures and guide the waters wherever they drain.'
translations.idiomatic: Breaching Yan–Yu eastern dikes could steer runoff downhill.

sentences.zh: 交令饑者盡得水產之饒，百姓不出境界之內，旦暮野食，此目下日給之益也。

translations.literal: 'Further order the hungry to enjoy fully the bounty of aquatic produce; so long as the common people do not leave their borders, they may eat from the wild morning and evening—this is the immediate daily provision.'
translations.idiomatic: Let refugees forage wetlands inside their home counties—that feeds today.

sentences.zh: 水去之後，填淤之田，畝收數鐘。

translations.literal: 'After the water recedes, the silted fields will yield several zhong per mu.'
translations.idiomatic: Once floodwaters fell, silted acres could yield several zhong per mu.

sentences.zh: 至春大種五穀，五穀必豐，此又明年益也。

translations.literal: 'Come spring, plant the five grains on a large scale and they will surely be abundant—this is next year's gain.'
translations.idiomatic: Spring grain on those flats would repay the breach next harvest.

sentences.zh: 臣前啟，典牧種牛不供耕駕，至於老不穿鼻者，無益於用，而徒有吏士穀草之費，歲送任駕者甚少，尚復不調習，宜大出賣，以易穀及為賞直。

translations.literal: 'Your servant earlier reported that the herd office's breeding oxen did not serve for ploughing or draft; as for those so old they were never nose-ringed, they are useless while wasting clerks' and soldiers' grain and fodder; each year very few are sent for draft duty and they are still not trained—they should be sold off in large numbers to exchange for grain and for reward payments.'
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu renewed his plea to sell off breeding oxen that never pulled a plough—herds that only consumed state fodder without adding use.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「孳育之物，不宜減散。

translations.literal: An edict replied: 'Creatures bred for increase ought not be reduced and scattered.'
translations.idiomatic: The court refused: breeding stock must not be dispersed.

sentences.zh: 」事遂停寢。

translations.literal: 'The matter thereupon halted.'
translations.idiomatic: The proposal died.

sentences.zh: 問主者，今典虞右典牧種產牛，大小相通，有四萬五千餘頭。

translations.literal: 'Asked of the responsible officials, the herd office and right herd now keep breeding oxen—large and small reckoned together—more than forty-five thousand head.'
translations.idiomatic: Officials counted forty-five thousand breeding cattle on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 苟不益世用，頭數雖多，其費日廣。

translations.literal: 'If they do not augment worldly use, though the head count is large, the expense grows daily.'
translations.idiomatic: Without productive work, head count only bled money.

sentences.zh: 古者匹馬丘牛，居則以耕，出則以戰，非如豬羊類也。

translations.literal: 'In antiquity a single horse or hill ox served at home for ploughing and abroad for war—they are not like pigs or sheep.'
translations.idiomatic: Ancient oxen ploughed at peace and pulled wagons at war—not barnyard pork.

sentences.zh: 今徒養宜用之牛，終為無用之費，甚失事宜。

translations.literal: 'Now to feed oxen that ought to be usable ends as useless expense—a grave mismatch with what is fitting.'
translations.idiomatic: Idle oxen broke both budget and precedent.

sentences.zh: 東南以水田為業，人無牛犢。

translations.literal: 'The southeast depends on paddy fields for its livelihood; people lack calves and oxen.'
translations.idiomatic: The southeast lived by paddy but lacked cattle.

sentences.zh: 今既壞陂，可分種牛三萬五千頭，以付二州將吏士庶，使及春耕。

translations.literal: 'Now that the weirs are ruined, we may divide out thirty-five thousand head of breeding oxen and assign them to officers, soldiers, and commoners of the two prefectures so they catch the spring ploughing.'
translations.idiomatic: With dikes failing, thirty-five thousand head could equip spring ploughing for two prefectures.

sentences.zh: 穀登之後，頭責三百斛。

translations.literal: 'After the grain is harvested, collect three hundred hu per head.'
translations.idiomatic: Tax back three hundred hu per ox after harvest.

sentences.zh: 是為化無用之費，得運水次成穀七百萬斛，此又數年後之益也。

translations.literal: 'That turns useless expense into seven million hu of grain transported to waterside depots—gain again for years to come.'
translations.idiomatic: Sell the herd for seven million hu delivered riverside—years of returns.

sentences.zh: 加以百姓降丘宅土，將來公私之饒乃不可計。

translations.literal: 'Add to this the common people descending hills and choosing high ground; future abundance for public and private purposes will be beyond reckoning.'
translations.idiomatic: Add hill dwellers resettling drier ground—public and private wealth would compound.

sentences.zh: 其所留好種萬頭，可即令右典牧都尉官屬養之。

translations.literal: 'The ten thousand head of good breeding stock retained may at once be entrusted to the right herd commandant's staff to pasture them.'
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand prime breeders could stay under the right herd commandant.

sentences.zh: 人多畜少，可並佃牧地，明其考課。

translations.literal: 'Where people are many and livestock few, they may jointly tenant pasture lands with clear inspection and assessment.'
translations.idiomatic: Crowded districts could share pasture with audited rotations.

sentences.zh: 此又三魏近甸，歲當復入數十萬斛穀，牛又皆當調習，動可駕用，皆今日之可全者也。」

translations.literal: 'This again means the three Wei capital districts and nearby suburbs will each year return several hundred thousand hu of grain; the oxen will all be trained for draft and readily harnessed—things that can be secured today in full.'
translations.idiomatic: The three Wei capital belts would repay hundreds of thousands of hu yearly once oxen learned the yoke—gains available immediately.

sentences.zh: 預又言：

translations.literal: Yu further stated:
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu added:

sentences.zh: 諸欲修水田者，皆以火耕水耨為便。

translations.literal: All who wish to repair paddy fields deem fire-ploughing and water-weeding convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Engineers fixing paddies loved slash-and-flood routines.

sentences.zh: 非不爾也，然此事施于新田草萊，與百姓居相絕離者耳。

translations.literal: It is not that this is wrong, yet the method applies only to new fields in wild scrub cut off from where commoners dwell.
translations.idiomatic: That works only for virgin bush far from villages—not crowded flood plains.

sentences.zh: 往者東南草創人稀，故得火田之利。

translations.literal: Formerly the southeast was newly opened and people were sparse, so slash-and-burn fields paid off.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jiangdong was empty enough that fire farming still worked.

sentences.zh: 自頃戶口日增，而陂堨歲決，良田變生蒲葦，人居沮澤之際，水陸失宜，放牧絕種，樹木立枯，皆陂之害也。

translations.literal: Recently household registers swell daily while dikes burst every year; good fields turn to rushes and reeds; men dwell on soggy margins where land and water fit poorly; pasturing fails and trees stand dead—all harm from over-diking.
translations.idiomatic: Population packed in while dams yearly failed—prime dirt went to marsh reed, villages squatted in mud, herds and orchards died behind leaky banks.

sentences.zh: 陂多則土薄水淺，潦不下潤。

translations.literal: Where dikes multiply the soil grows thin and water shallow; soaking rains cannot sink deep.
translations.idiomatic: Too many ponds meant thin topsoil and perched water—rain never soaked through.

sentences.zh: 故每有水雨，輒復橫流，延及陸田。

translations.literal: Therefore whenever storm-water fell it flooded sideways out onto dry-field plots.
translations.idiomatic: Every storm sheeted across upland farms.

sentences.zh: 言者不思其故，因云此土不可陸種。

translations.literal: Speakers never pondered the cause and therefore claimed this soil could not be dry-farmed.
translations.idiomatic: Critics blamed the dirt instead of the dams.

sentences.zh: 臣計漢之戶口，以驗今之陂處，皆陸業也。

translations.literal: Your servant reckons Han household figures against today's diked sites—they were all dry-field enterprises.
translations.idiomatic: Han census maps show those acres had once been upland grain.

sentences.zh: 其或有舊陂舊堨，則堅完修固，非今所謂當為人害者也。

translations.literal: Where old ponds and old weirs remain, keep them soundly repaired; they are not what today should be deemed harmful to people.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient tanks still holding water deserve upkeep—not the same as recent mistakes.

sentences.zh: 臣前見尚書胡威啟宜壞陂，其言懇至。

translations.literal: Your servant earlier saw Minister Director Hu Wei memorialize that certain dikes ought to be breached; his words were utterly earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Wei had already pleaded earnestly to breach the worst impoundments.

sentences.zh: 臣中者又見宋侯相應遵上便宜，求壞泗陂，徙運道。

translations.literal: Among mid-level officials your servant also saw District Minister Ying Zun of Song county submit a convenience memorial requesting breaching the Si weir and shifting the transport route.
translations.idiomatic: District aide Ying Zun paired a shorter canal route with draining the Si reservoir.

sentences.zh: 時下都督度支共處當，各據所見，不從遵言。

translations.literal: The regional commandant and budget director jointly deliberated; each clung to his own view and refused Zun's advice.
translations.idiomatic: Area command and finance vetoed him by committee.

sentences.zh: 臣案遵上事，運道東詣壽春，有舊渠，可不由泗陂。

translations.literal: Your servant has reviewed Zun's submission: the transport route east to Shouchun uses an old channel and need not pass the Si weir.
translations.idiomatic: Zun was right—an older channel reached Shouchun without the Si pond.

sentences.zh: 泗陂在遵地界壞地凡萬三千餘頃，傷敗成業。

translations.literal: The Si weir, lying within Zun's jurisdiction, damages more than thirteen thousand qing of cropland and ruins established farms.
translations.idiomatic: That dike drowned thirteen thousand qing inside his county.

sentences.zh: 遵縣領應佃二千六百口，可謂至少，而猶患地狹，不足肆力，此皆水之為害也。

translations.literal: Zun's district registers only twenty-six hundred tenant households—the smallest tally—yet still complains the ground is cramped and labor cannot stretch; all this is water's harm.
translations.idiomatic: Even a sparse county could not expand plots—pure hydraulic choke.

sentences.zh: 當所共恤，而都督度支方復執異，非所見之難，直以不同害理也。

translations.literal: This ought to concern everyone alike, yet commandant and budget director still cling to opposing views—not because the facts are hard to see but because they straight refuse common sense.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone should share the fix; headquarters obstruction was ideology, not evidence.

sentences.zh: 人心所見既不同，利害之情又有異。

translations.literal: Once men's views differ, calculations of gain and harm diverge too.
translations.idiomatic: Split opinions split cost-benefit math.

sentences.zh: 軍家之與郡縣，士大夫之與百姓，其意莫有同者，此皆偏其利以忘其害者也。

translations.literal: Between army colonies and civil counties, between gentlemen and commoners, scarcely anyone agrees—all seize partial profit and forget shared injury.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison, prefect, scholar, and farmer each chase narrow gain and ignore collective ruin.

sentences.zh: 此理之所以未盡，而事之所以多患也。

translations.literal: That is why principle stays unfinished and affairs breed endless trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Hence policy stalls and crises multiply.

sentences.zh: 臣又案，豫州界二度支所領佃者，州郡大軍雜士，凡用水田七千五百餘頃耳，計三年之儲，不過二萬餘頃。

translations.literal: Your servant further notes that within Yu Province the two budget offices supervise tenants—troops and miscellaneous labor from prefectures total only seventy-five hundred qing of paddy; reckoning three years of reserves, they fall short of twenty thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Province's fiscal colonies irrigate under seventy-six hundred qing—three years of grain still misses twenty thousand qing stored.

sentences.zh: 以常理言之，無為多積無用之水，況於今者水澇湓溢，大為災害。

translations.literal: By ordinary reckoning one ought not pile useless water; how much more today when floods surge and cause vast disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Plain arithmetic forbids hoarding useless ponds—especially under megafloods.

sentences.zh: 臣以為與其失當，寧瀉之不滀。

translations.literal: Your servant believes that rather than mismanage storage, better drain than dam.
translations.idiomatic: Better drain outright than mis-store.

sentences.zh: 宜發明詔，敕刺史二千石，其漢氏舊陂舊堨及山谷私家小陂，皆當修繕以積水。

translations.literal: Issue an explicit edict charging prefects and two-thousand-bushel officials that Han-era ponds and mountain ravine pools held by private families must all be repaired to hold water.
translations.idiomatic: Publish orders: restore legitimate Han tanks and private hill ponds while auditing outlets.

sentences.zh: 其諸魏氏以來所造立，及諸因雨決溢蒲葦馬腸陂之類，皆決瀝之。

translations.literal: Everything built since Wei or breached by rains into reed-choked horse-gut marshes—breach and drain them all.
translations.idiomatic: Break Wei-era vanity dikes and accidental reed lakes.

sentences.zh: 長吏二千石躬親勸功，諸食力之人並一時附功令，比及水凍，得粗枯涸，其所修功實之人皆以俾之。

translations.literal: Let two-thousand-bushel magistrates personally urge the work; every laborer joins under emergency statute; before ice seals the flow, achieve rough draw-down; reward men according to actual accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates lead winter crews under emergency law; drain before freeze-up; pay wages to proven workers.

sentences.zh: 其舊陂堨溝渠當有所補塞者，皆尋求微跡，一如漢時故事，豫為部分列上，須冬，東南休兵交代，各留一月以佐之。

translations.literal: Where old dikes and ditches need plugging, trace faint traces exactly like Han precedent; plan each sector in advance and memorialize; wait until winter when southeast armies rotate reliefs—each corps leaves one month of labor to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Patch legacy channels per Han surveys; schedule winter repairs when southeast garrisons rotate and lend a month's labor.

sentences.zh: 夫川瀆有常流，地形有定體，漢氏居人眾多，猶以無患，今因其所患而宣寫之，跡古事以明近，大理顯然，可坐論而得。

translations.literal: River courses keep steady flows and terrain fixed forms; Han settlers were numerous yet avoided calamity—now drain what harms by ancient analogy and recent proof lies clear enough to settle by discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Rivers keep beds; Han peasants thronged yet stayed dry—breaching repeats proven history.

sentences.zh: 臣不勝愚意，竊謂最是今日之實益也。

translations.literal: Your servant, overwhelmed by humble intent, privately thinks this is truly today's practical gain.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu believes draining beats debating.

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court accepted it.
