translations.idiomatic: Luoyang approved.

sentences.zh: 及平吳之後，有司又奏：「詔書『王公以國為家，京城不宜復有田宅。

translations.literal: After Wu was pacified, officials further memorialized: 'The edict states: Princes and dukes take their state as home—the capital ought not again hold field estates.'
translations.idiomatic: Post-conquest ministers cited edicts: princes should live off fiefs, not Luoyang acreage.

sentences.zh: 今未暇作諸國邸，當使城中有往來處，近郊有芻槁之田』。

translations.literal: 'We have not yet built each state's mansion; meanwhile let them have lodging inside the walls and fodder-field acreage on the near suburban fringe.'
translations.idiomatic: Until each prince had a manor, they needed urban quarters plus suburban hay plots.

sentences.zh: 今可限之，國王公侯，京城得有一宅之處。

translations.literal: 'Now issue caps: princes, dukes, and marquises may hold one mansion site inside the capital.'
translations.idiomatic: Cap each noble to one city residence.

sentences.zh: 近郊田，大國田十五頃，次國十頃，小國七頃。

translations.literal: 'Near suburbs award fields: great states fifteen qing, middle states ten qing, small states seven qing.'
translations.idiomatic: Rank land grants at fifteen, ten, or seven qing by kingdom size.

sentences.zh: 城內無宅城外有者，皆聽留之。」

translations.literal: 'Those without dwellings inside the walls but holding land outside may keep them.'
translations.idiomatic: Nobles owning only suburban farms could stay.

sentences.zh: 又制戶調之式：丁男之戶，歲輸絹三匹，綿三斤，女及次丁男為戶者半輸。

translations.literal: They also codified household levy formulae: adult-male households annually rendered three bolts of tabby and three jin of floss; households headed by women or secondary adult males paid half.
translations.idiomatic: Household taxes fixed three bolts plus three jin for adult males; female-headed halved it.

sentences.zh: 其諸邊郡或三分之二，遠者三分之一。

translations.literal: Frontier commanderies paid two thirds or one third on distant tiers.
translations.idiomatic: Border counties paid two-thirds or one-third rates by distance.

sentences.zh: 夷人輸賨布，戶一匹，遠者或一丈。

translations.literal: Yi tribes rendered tribute cloth—one bolt per household, sometimes one zhang for remote bands.
translations.idiomatic: Non-Han households paid tribute cloth—one bolt, or one zhang farther out.

sentences.zh: 男子一人占田七十畝，女子三十畝。

translations.literal: One adult male might claim seventy mu of land; a woman thirty mu.
translations.idiomatic: Allocation ceilings ran seventy mu per man, thirty per woman.

sentences.zh: 其外丁男課田五十畝，丁女二十畝，次丁男半之，女則不課。

translations.literal: Beyond that, liable adult males owed fifty mu of assessed tillage, liable females twenty mu; secondary adult males paid half; women otherwise owed none.
translations.idiomatic: Taxable assignment: fifty mu for men, twenty for liable women, half for youths—other women exempt.

sentences.zh: 男女年十六已上至六十為正丁，十五已下至十三、六十一已上至六十五為次丁，十二已下六十六已上為老小，不事。

translations.literal: Males and females aged sixteen through sixty counted as primary adults; thirteen through fifteen and sixty-one through sixty-five were secondary adults; twelve and below or sixty-six and above were old or young and owed no labor.
translations.idiomatic: Primary adults spanned sixteen to sixty; teens and early seniors were secondary; children and elders skipped service.

sentences.zh: 遠夷不課田者輸義米，戶三斛，遠者五斗，極遠者輸算錢，人二十八文。

translations.literal: Remote Yi who did not owe field tax rendered 'righteous grain'—three hu per household, five dou in middling distance, twenty-eight cash poll tax for the farthest.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier tribes paid symbolic grain—three hu default, tapering to poll cash.

sentences.zh: 其官品第一至於第九，各以貴賤占田，品第一者占五十頃，第二品四十五頃，第三品四十頃，第四品三十五頃，第五品三十頃，第六品二十五頃，第七品二十頃，第八品十五頃，第九品十頃。

translations.literal: Official ranks one through nine each claimed fields by nobility: rank one fifty qing, rank two forty-five, rank three forty, rank four thirty-five, rank five thirty, rank six twenty-five, rank seven twenty, rank eight fifteen, rank nine ten.
translations.idiomatic: Nine-rank officials carved fifty down to ten qing by grade.

sentences.zh: 而又各以品之高卑廕其親屬，多者及九族，少者三世。

translations.literal: Moreover each rank sheltered kin by status—widest privilege embraced nine branches of kin, narrowest three generations.
translations.idiomatic: Each grade sheltered kin across nine lines or three by seniority.

sentences.zh: 宗室、國賓、先賢之後及士人子孫亦如之。

translations.literal: Imperial clan, state guests, descendants of former worthies, and sons of scholars followed the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Royals, honored houses, and scholar lines matched those shelters.

sentences.zh: 而又得廕人以為衣食客及佃客，品第六已上得衣食客三人，第七第八品二人，第九品及舉輦、跡禽、前驅、由基、強弩、司馬、羽林郎、殿中冗從武賁、殿中武賁、持椎斧武騎武賁、持鈒冗從武賁、命中武賁武騎一人。

translations.literal: They could also register dependents as cloth-and-food clients or tenant clients: ranks six and above kept three cloth-and-food clients; ranks seven and eight two; rank nine plus palanquin crew, fowl trackers, outrunners, master archers, strong-crossbow majors, Feathered Forest guards, supernumerary corridor halberdiers, palace halberdiers, mace-bearing halberd cavalry, extra attendant halberdiers, and crack-shot halberdiers—one man each.
translations.idiomatic: Salary slots extended to registered bondsmen—three clients for sixth rank and above, tapering to one for petty guards and cadet halberdiers.

sentences.zh: 其應有佃客者，官品第一第二者佃客無過五十戶，第三品十戶，第四品七戶，第五品五戶，第六品三戶，第七品二戶，第八品第九品一戶。

translations.literal: Where tenant clients applied: ranks one and two might hold fifty tenant households at most; rank three ten households; rank four seven; rank five five; rank six three; rank seven two; ranks eight and nine one.
translations.idiomatic: Tenant quotas scaled from fifty households for top ministers to one for lowest nobles.

sentences.zh: 是時天下無事，賦稅平均，人咸安其業而樂其事。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was tranquil, taxes even, and everyone rested content in his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Peace brought balanced levies and satisfied farmers.

sentences.zh: 及惠帝之後，政教陵夷，至於永嘉，喪亂彌甚。

translations.literal: After Emperor Hui, governance slid downhill until Yongjia, when catastrophe deepened.
translations.idiomatic: Post-Hui decay peaked at Yongjia's collapse.

sentences.zh: 雍州以東，人多饑乏，更相鬻賣，奔迸流移，不可勝數。

translations.literal: East of Yong Province multitudes starved, selling one another, fleeing, drifting—beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: East of Chang'an people pawned kin and scattered countless.

sentences.zh: 幽、并、司、冀、秦、雍六州大蝗，草木及牛馬毛皆盡。

translations.literal: You, Bing, Si, Ji, Qin, and Yong—six provinces—suffered locusts so dense they stripped grass, trees, even cattle and horse hair.
translations.idiomatic: Six northern provinces saw locusts eat every blade and bristle.

sentences.zh: 又大疾疫，兼以饑饉。

translations.literal: Great pestilence piled atop famine.
translations.idiomatic: Plague layered on hunger.

sentences.zh: 百姓又為寇賊所殺，流屍滿河，白骨蔽野。

translations.literal: Bandits also slaughtered commoners; floating corpses jammed the rivers; white bones carpeted the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Raids added corpses damming streams and whitening fields.

sentences.zh: 劉曜之逼，朝廷議欲遷都倉垣。

translations.literal: Pressed by Liu Yao, court debated moving the capital to Cangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao's advance forced a Cangyuan relocation debate.

sentences.zh: 人多相食，饑疫總至，百官流亡者十八九。

translations.literal: People ate one another; famine and plague arrived together; eight or nine of every ten officials fled.
translations.idiomatic: Cannibalism met epidemic while nine-tenths of the bureaucracy ran.

sentences.zh: 元帝為晉王，課督農功，詔二千石長吏以入穀多少為殿最。

translations.literal: When Yuan Di was Prince of Jin he assessed farming performance and ordered two-thousand-bushel magistrates ranked by grain intake.
translations.idiomatic: As prince, Yuan Di graded prefects on harvest figures.

sentences.zh: 其非宿衛要任，皆宜赴農，使軍各自佃作，即以為廩。

translations.literal: All who were not capital guards on vital duty should join farming; each army would colonize its own fields and draw rations therefrom.
translations.idiomatic: Nonessential troops farmed for their own mess halls.

sentences.zh: ，詔曰：「徐、揚二州土宜三麥，可督令地，投秋下種，至夏而熟，繼新故之交，于以周濟，所益甚大。

translations.literal: An edict followed: 'Xu and Yang provinces suit winter wheat—urge appropriate lands sown in autumn to ripen by summer, bridging old and new grain; relief value will be immense.'
translations.idiomatic: An edict pushed autumn wheat on Xu–Yang soils to bridge crop seasons.

sentences.zh: 昔漢遣輕車使者氾勝之督三輔種麥，而關中遂穰。

translations.literal: Formerly Han sent mobile envoy Fan Shengzhi to supervise triple-capital wheat planting and Guanzhong grew abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Han once sent Fan Shengzhi to triple-capital wheat trials—Guanzhong flourished.

sentences.zh: 勿令後晚。

translations.literal: Do not allow late sowing.
translations.idiomatic: Ban tardy planting.

sentences.zh: 」其後頻年麥雖有旱蝗，而為益猶多。

translations.literal: Although drought and locusts struck wheat years repeatedly, the gain still outweighed loss.
translations.idiomatic: Even drought-year wheat beat nothing.

sentences.zh: 二年，三吳大饑，死者以百數，吳郡太守鄧攸輒開倉廩賑之。

translations.literal: In the second year the three Wu commanderies suffered great famine; dead numbered in the hundreds; Wu commandery governor Deng You opened granaries without asking.
translations.idiomatic: Second-year Jiangnan famine killed hundreds until Deng You broke granaries.

sentences.zh: 元帝時使黃門侍郎虞、桓彝開倉廩振給，並省眾役。

translations.literal: Under Yuan Di, Attendant Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate Yu Tan and Huan Yi opened granaries for relief and cut miscellaneous labor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Di tasked Yu Tan and Huan Yi to dispense grain and cut corvée.

sentences.zh: 百官各上封事，後軍將軍應詹表曰：「夫一人不耕，天下必有受其饑者。

translations.literal: The hundred officials each submitted sealed memorials; Rear Army General Ying Zhan stated: 'If one man does not plough, someone under Heaven goes hungry.'
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhan warned: one idle plough meant nationwide hunger.

sentences.zh: 而軍興以來，征戰運漕，朝廷宗廟，百官用度，既已殷廣，下及工商流寓僮僕不親農桑而遊食者，以十萬計。

translations.literal: Since armies mobilized, campaigns and transport, court and shrines, official budgets have swollen vastly; meanwhile artisans, merchants, refugees, and domestic servants who neither farm nor tend silk yet wander for food number in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: War spending exploded while hundreds of thousands of urban idlers skipped the soil.

sentences.zh: 不思開立美利，而望國足人給，豈不難哉！

translations.literal: Yet you plot no splendid profit while expecting the state full and people fed—how difficult!
translations.idiomatic: Expecting plenty without opening revenue defies logic.

sentences.zh: 古人言曰，饑寒並至，雖堯舜不能使野無寇盜；

translations.literal: The ancients said: when cold and hunger arrive together, even Yao and Shun cannot keep the wilds free of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient wisdom: cold hunger breeds bandits even under sage kings.

sentences.zh: 貧富並兼，雖皋陶不能使強不陵弱。

translations.literal: 'When rich and poor polarize, even Gao Yao cannot stop the strong from bullying the weak.'
translations.idiomatic: Extremes let bullies prey—no judge fixes that imbalance.

sentences.zh: 故有國有家者，何嘗不務農重穀。

translations.literal: Therefore holders of state and household have never neglected farming and grain.
translations.idiomatic: States survive by prizing grain.

sentences.zh: 近魏武皇帝用棗祗、韓浩之議，廣建屯田，又於征伐之中，分帶甲之士，隨宜開墾，故下不甚勞，而大功克舉也。

translations.literal: Recently Emperor Wu of Wei adopted Zao Zhi and Han Hao's advice, broadly establishing agricultural colonies; amid campaigns he also detached armored troops to clear land as suited—therefore the lower ranks felt little fatigue yet great deeds succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's colony counsel fed armies without exhausting peasants.

sentences.zh: 間者流人奔東吳，東吳今儉，皆已還反。

translations.literal: Lately refugees fled east to Wu; Wu is now lean and they have all returned.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees who fled to Wu drifted home when Wu tightened.

sentences.zh: 江西良田，曠廢未久，火耕水耨，為功差易。

translations.literal: Good fields west of the Yangzi lie waste only briefly—slash-and-burn works there with relative ease.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi's idle acres suit quick fire-and-flood clearing.

sentences.zh: 宜簡流人，興復農官，功勞報賞，皆如魏氏故事。

translations.literal: Select drift people, revive farming offices, reward merit by precedent of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Reset wanderers under Wei-style farm bureaus with merit pay.

sentences.zh: 一年中與百姓，二年分稅，三年計賦稅以使之，公私兼濟，則倉盈庾億，可計日而待也。

translations.literal: First year distribute to commoners; second year split tax; third year reckon full levy—such mutual relief fills bins sooner than counting days.
translations.idiomatic: Year-one grants, year-two split levies, year-three full tax—fills granaries fast.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「昔高祖使蕭何鎮關中，光武令寇恂守河內，魏武委鐘繇以西事，故能使八表夷蕩，區內輯寧。

translations.literal: He added: 'Formerly Gaozu had Xiao He secure Guanzhong; Guangwu ordered Kou Xun to hold Hanoi; Emperor Wu of Wei entrusted Zhong Yao with western affairs—thus the eight directions were swept calm and the interior rested.'
translations.idiomatic: He cited Xiao He, Kou Xun, and Zhong Yao anchoring interior bases.

sentences.zh: 今中州蕭條，未蒙疆理，此兆庶所以企望。

translations.literal: Now the central plain lies waste and ungoverned—the myriad people crane their necks hoping.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland still waits for reconstruction.

sentences.zh: 壽春一方之會，去此不遠，宜選都督有文武經略者，遠以振河洛之形勢，近以為徐豫之籓鎮，綏集流散，使人有攸依，專委農功，令事有所局。

translations.literal: Shouchun anchors one quadrant and lies near—choose a regional governor versed in civil and military strategy to shake Heluo's posture far off and shield Xu-Yu near at hand; gather wanderers so men have shelter; concentrate on farming so tasks stay bounded.
translations.idiomatic: Fortify Shouchun with a strategist who revives Huai River farms and shelters refugees.

sentences.zh: 趙充國農于金城，以平西零；

translations.literal: Zhao Chongguo farmed Jincheng to pacify the western Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chongguo's Jincheng colonies broke the western tribes.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮耕於渭濱，規抗上國。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang ploughed along the Wei River planning resistance to the superior state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang's Wei River farms sustained northern defense.

sentences.zh: 今諸軍自不對敵，皆宜齊課。

translations.literal: Now every army not engaged with the enemy alike ought to follow uniform assessments.
translations.idiomatic: Idle legions should face identical farm quotas.

sentences.zh: ，成帝始度百姓田，取十分之一，率畝稅米三升。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng began surveying commoners' fields he took one tenth, generally three sheng of rice per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's field survey taxed one-tenth—three sheng rice per mu.

sentences.zh: 六年，以海賊寇抄，運漕不繼，發王公以下餘丁，各運米六斛。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, because pirates raided transport and grain fleets stalled, they drafted surplus males from princes downward, each to haul six hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Year six piracy stalled convoys—nobles' spare males hauled six hu each.

sentences.zh: 是後頻年水災旱蝗，田收不至。

translations.literal: Thereafter flood, drought, and locusts struck repeatedly and harvests failed to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Years of disaster gutted yields.

sentences.zh: 咸康初，算度田稅米，空懸五十餘萬斛，尚書褚裒以下免官。

translations.literal: At Xiankang's opening they reckoned field-tax rice and found more than five hundred thousand hu missing on the books; Minister Director Chu Pou downward were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiankang audits exposed over five hundred thousand hu missing from ledgers—ministers fell.

sentences.zh: 穆帝之世，頻有大軍，糧運不繼，制王公以下十三戶共借一人，助度支運。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Mu great armies mobilized often while grain transport failed; regulations drafted one laborer per thirteen households from princes downward to assist budget convoys.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's wars drafted one porter per thirteen households.

sentences.zh: 升平初，荀羨為北府都督，鎮下邳，起田于東陽之石鱉，公私利之。

translations.literal: At Shengping's opening Xun Xian became northern headquarters commandant at Xiapi, opening fields east of Dongyang at Stone Turtle—public and private both profited.
translations.idiomatic: Shengping saw Xun Xian's Stone Turtle paddy enrich Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 哀帝即位，乃減田租，畝收二升。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai ascended he reduced land rent to two sheng per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Ai cut acre rent to two sheng.

sentences.zh: 孝武，除度田收租之制，王公以下口稅三斛，唯蠲在役之身。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu abolished the surveyed-field rent system; from princes downward each mouth owed three hu grain tax, exempt only those actively serving.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu junked acre assessments for a three-hu head tax with service exemptions.

sentences.zh: 八年，又增稅米，口五石。

translations.literal: In the eighth year they again increased grain tax to five shi per mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Year eight raised per-capita grain to five shi.

sentences.zh: 至於末年，天下無事，時和年豐，百姓樂業，穀帛殷阜，幾乎家給人足矣。

translations.literal: By his closing years the realm was calm, seasons mild and harvests rich; common people prospered in their trades; grain and silk piled high until nearly every household had enough.
translations.idiomatic: Late Xiaowu brought peace, bumper bins, and near self-sufficiency.

sentences.zh: 漢錢舊用五銖，自王莽改革，百姓皆不便之。

translations.literal: Han coinage traditionally used wushu cash; from Wang Mang's reforms onward commoners found everything inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Han five-zhu coin vanished under Wang Mang's monetary chaos.

sentences.zh: 及公孫述僭號於蜀，童謠曰：「黃牛白腹，五銖當復。

translations.literal: When Gongsun Shu illegally proclaimed himself in Shu, a children's rhyme ran: 'Yellow ox, white belly—the five zhū shall return.'
translations.idiomatic: Shu children sang that white-bellied cattle meant returning five-zhu cash.

sentences.zh: 」好事者竊言，王莽稱黃，述欲繼之，故稱白帝。

translations.literal: Busybodies whispered that Wang Mang styled himself 'yellow' while Shu claimed to succeed him and styled the White Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Gossip tied yellow Wang Mang to white-clad Shu.

sentences.zh: 五銖漢貨，言漢當復並天下也。

translations.literal: The five zhū was Han currency—it meant Han would reunite the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Five-zhu stood for Han restoration.

sentences.zh: 至光武中興，除莽貨泉。

translations.literal: When Guangwu restored Han he abolished Mang's 'goods springs.'
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu voided Mang's token notes.

sentences.zh: ，馬援又上書曰：「富國之本，在於食貨，宜如舊鑄五銖錢。

translations.literal: Ma Yuan further memorialized: 'The root of enriching the state lies in food and currency—mint wushu coin as of old.'
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuan urged restoring five-zhu metal.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是復鑄五銖錢，天下以為便。

translations.literal: Thereupon they recast wushu coinage and the realm deemed it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Restored five-zhu coin satisfied markets.

sentences.zh: 及章帝時，穀帛價貴，縣官經用不足，朝廷憂之。

translations.literal: By Emperor Zhang's reign grain and silk grew dear; official budgets ran short and court worried.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's era faced dear grain and empty treasuries.

sentences.zh: 尚書張林言：「今非但穀貴也，百物皆貴，此錢賤故爾。

translations.literal: Minister Director Zhang Lin stated: 'Today not only grain is dear—every commodity is—because cash is cheap.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin blamed cheap copper for universal inflation.

sentences.zh: 宜令天下悉以布帛為租，市買皆用之，封錢勿出，如此則錢少物皆賤矣。

translations.literal: 'Order the realm to pay rent in cloth and silk, conduct markets in kind, seal coin away from circulation—then cash grows scarce and goods cheapen.'
translations.idiomatic: He proposed cloth rents and hoarding bronze.

sentences.zh: 又，鹽者食之急也，縣官可自賣鹽，武帝時施行之，名曰均輸。

translations.literal: 'Moreover salt is urgent for food; the government may sell salt itself—Emperor Wu practiced this under the name equitable delivery.'
translations.idiomatic: State salt sales echoed Emperor Wu's junshu schemes.

sentences.zh: 」於是事下尚書通議。

translations.literal: The matter thereupon went down to the Ministry Director's general deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to joint ministry review.

sentences.zh: 尚書硃暉議曰：「王制，天子不言有無，諸侯不言多少，食祿者不與百姓爭利。

translations.literal: Minister Director Zhu Hui argued: 'The royal regulations say: the Son of Heaven does not speak of having or lacking; feudal lords do not speak of more or less; salary recipients do not contend with commoners for profit.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hui cited ritual: rulers do not haggle markets with peasants.

sentences.zh: 均輸之法，與賈販無異。

translations.literal: Equitable-delivery policy differs in no way from peddling.
translations.idiomatic: State junshu peddling mimicked street hawkers.

sentences.zh: 以布帛為租，則吏多奸。

translations.literal: If rent is paid in cloth and silk, clerks will multiply fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Bolt-and-floss taxes invited clerk theft.

sentences.zh: 官自賣鹽，與下爭利，非明王所宜行。

translations.literal: The government selling salt itself wrests profit from subjects—a thing no enlightened king should practice.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial salt shops stole retailers' margin.

sentences.zh: 」帝本以林言為是，得暉議，因發怒，遂用林言，少時復止。

translations.literal: The emperor had originally deemed Zhang Lin correct; when he received Zhu Hui's opinion he grew angry, followed Lin anyway, yet soon rescinded the policy.
translations.idiomatic: The throne flipped from Zhang Lin to Zhu Hui and back—salt reform died young.

sentences.zh: 桓帝時有上書言：「人以貨輕錢薄，故致貧困，宜改鑄大錢。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Huan a memorial stated: 'Because goods are dear and cash thin, people sink into poverty—large cash should be recast.'
translations.idiomatic: Huan's court heard that debased coin caused poverty—mint bigger money.

sentences.zh: 」事下四府群僚及太學能言之士。

translations.literal: The matter went down to the four chief offices' staffs and eloquent scholars of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Policy hit the four ministries and Taixue debaters.

sentences.zh: 孝廉劉陶上議曰：

translations.literal: Filial-and-incorrupt nominee Liu Tao submitted an opinion:
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tao answered the mint debate.

sentences.zh: 臣伏讀鑄錢之詔，平輕重之義，訪覃幽微，不遺窮賤，是以藿食之人，謬延逮及。

translations.literal: 'Your servant has knelt to read the coinage edict balancing light and heavy meaning; inquiry reaches even the hidden and lowly—thus humble grain-eaters were wrongly admitted to respond.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tao thanked the edict for polling even commoners.

sentences.zh: 蓋以當今之憂，不在於貨，在乎人饑。

translations.literal: 'In sum today's worry lies not in goods but in human hunger.'
translations.idiomatic: Hunger trumped currency.

sentences.zh: 是以先王觀象育物，敬授民時，使男不逋畝，女不下機，故君臣之道行，王路之教通。

translations.literal: 'Therefore former kings observed celestial patterns to nurture things and reverently handed down seasons to the people, so men did not flee the furrows and women did not leave the loom—thus ruler-minister conduct prevailed and royal instruction spread.'
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity synchronized calendars so men farmed and women wove.

sentences.zh: 由是言之，食者乃有國之所寶，百姓之至貴也。

translations.literal: 'From this perspective food is what makes a state precious and commoners supreme.'
translations.idiomatic: Grain, not bronze, anchors the realm.

sentences.zh: 竊以比年已來，良苗盡於蝗螟之口，杼柚空於公私之求。

translations.literal: 'Your servant privately notes that in recent years fine sprouts have been eaten up by locusts and caterpillars while shuttles stand empty under public and private exactions.'
translations.idiomatic: Locusts ate shoots while taxes emptied looms.

sentences.zh: 所急朝夕之食，所患靡盬之事，豈謂錢之厚薄，銖兩之輕重哉！

translations.literal: 'What we urgently need is morning-and-evening food; what we fear are unfinished tasks—how can this concern coin thickness or weight!'
translations.idiomatic: Bellies matter—not mintage specs.

sentences.zh: 就使當今沙礫化為南金，瓦石變為和玉，使百姓渴無所飲，饑無所食，雖皇羲之純德，唐虞之文明，猶不能以保蕭牆之內也。

translations.literal: 'Suppose gravel turned to southern gold and tile-stone to polished jade yet commoners had nothing to drink when thirsty and nothing to eat when hungry—even Fu Xi's pure virtue or Tang-Yu's brilliance could not preserve peace inside the curtain-wall palace.'
translations.idiomatic: Gold paving starving streets buys no loyalty.

sentences.zh: 蓋百姓可百年無貨，不可以一朝有饑，故食為至急也。

translations.literal: 'Commoners may lack goods for a century but cannot endure hunger one dawn—therefore food is supremely urgent.'
translations.idiomatic: People endure poverty of coin, never of rice.

sentences.zh: 議者不達農殖之本，多言鑄冶之便，或欲因緣行詐，以賈國利。

translations.literal: 'Critics miss the root of farming yet harp on minting convenience; some scheme fraud to milk state profit.'
translations.idiomatic: Mint lobbyists ignored tillage.

sentences.zh: 國利將盡，取者爭競，造鑄之端，於是乎生。

translations.literal: 'When state profit nears exhaustion claimants contend—minting quarrels arise from this.'
translations.idiomatic: When treasury thins, mint politics erupts.

sentences.zh: 蓋萬人鑄之，一人奪之，猶不能給，況今一人鑄之則萬人奪之乎！

translations.literal: 'If ten thousand men mint and one man seizes the yield, supply still fails—how much less when one mints and ten thousand seize!'
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand furnaces cannot feed one hoarder.

sentences.zh: 雖以陰陽為炭，萬物為銅，役不食之民，使不饑之士，猶不能足無厭之求也。

translations.literal: 'Even taking yin and yang for charcoal and the myriad things for copper, employing men who do not eat and officers who do not hunger, still cannot satisfy bottomless demand.'
translations.idiomatic: No furnace satisfies infinite greed.

sentences.zh: 夫欲民財殷阜，要在止役禁奪，則百姓不勞而足。

translations.literal: 'Desiring people's wealth ample hinges on stopping labor levies and forbidding seizure—then commoners gain plenty without toil.'
translations.idiomatic: End corvée and predation—wealth follows.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖德，湣海內之憂戚，傷天下之艱難，欲鑄錢齊貨，以救其弊，此猶養魚沸鼎之中，棲鳥列火之上。

translations.literal: 'Your Majesty's sagely virtue grieves at sorrow within the seas and hardship under Heaven, wishing to mint coin and equalize goods to heal these ills—this is like raising fish in a boiling cauldron or roosting birds atop piled flame.'
translations.idiomatic: Minting while peasants starve broils fish in steam.

sentences.zh: 木水，本魚鳥之所生也，用之不時，必至焦爛。

translations.literal: 'Wood and water are where fish and birds are born; used untimely they must end charred and rotten.'
translations.idiomatic: Misusing wood and water scorches the creatures they sustain.

sentences.zh: 願陛下寬鍥薄之禁，後冶鑄之議也。

translations.literal: 'May Your Majesty relax bans on petty carving and postpone smelting debates.'
translations.idiomatic: Delay mint schemes; loosen petty-tool bans.

sentences.zh: 帝竟不鑄錢。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end did not cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: The court dropped recoinage.

sentences.zh: 及獻帝初平中，董卓乃更鑄小錢，由是貨輕而物貴，穀一斛至錢數百萬。

translations.literal: By Emperor Xian's Chuping era Dong Zhuo recast inferior small cash; goods grew dear and currency light until one hu of grain cost millions of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Chuping debasement sent grain to millions per hu.

sentences.zh: 至魏武為相，於是罷之，還用五銖。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Wei became chancellor he abolished Zhuo's pieces and returned to wushu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao restored five-zhu coin.

sentences.zh: 是時不鑄錢既久，貨本不多，又更無增益，故穀賤無已。

translations.literal: At that time minting had long ceased; monetary stock was small and grew no further—therefore grain stayed cheap without end.
translations.idiomatic: Without fresh bronze, grain prices slid forever.

sentences.zh: 及，魏文帝罷五銖錢，使百姓以穀帛為市。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Wen of Wei abolished wushu coin and ordered commoners to trade by grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wendi voided metal for barter grain and bolts.

sentences.zh: 至明帝世，錢廢穀用既久，人間巧偽漸多，競濕穀以要利，作薄絹以為市，雖處以嚴刑而不能禁也。

translations.literal: By Emperor Ming's reign coin had lain idle and grain trade lasted so long that human trickery multiplied—people raced to dampen grain for profit and weave thin tabby for markets; harsh punishments could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mingdi watched soggy grain and tissue-thin silk defeat torture statutes.

sentences.zh: 司馬芝等舉朝大議，以為用錢非徒豐國，亦所以省刑。

translations.literal: Sima Zhi and others debated court-wide, holding that using coin not only enriched the state but also reduced punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhi argued coin fed treasury and emptied jails.

sentences.zh: 今若更鑄五銖錢，則國豐刑省，於事為便。

translations.literal: 'If we now recast wushu coin, the state grows rich and punishments lighten—convenient on every count.'
translations.idiomatic: Restoring five-zhu cuts fraud and fills bins.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝乃更立五銖錢，至晉用之，不聞有所改創。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei therefore re-established wushu coin; Jin continued using it without hearing of reform.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mingdi's five-zhu carried straight into Jin unchanged.

sentences.zh: 孫權，鑄大錢一當五百。

translations.literal: Sun Quan minted large coin valued at five hundred ordinary cash.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan struck heavy disks worth five hundred cash.

sentences.zh: ，又鑄當千錢。

translations.literal: He further minted thousand-cash denominations.
translations.idiomatic: He added thousand-to-one tokens.

sentences.zh: 故呂蒙定荊州，孫權賜錢一億。

translations.literal: Therefore when Lü Meng seized Jingzhou, Sun Quan rewarded him with one hundred million cash.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng's Jingzhou coup earned a hundred-million string bonus.

sentences.zh: 錢既太貴，但有空名，人間患之。

translations.literal: Because coin grew nominally dear yet lacked substance, people suffered under it.
translations.idiomatic: Nominal wealth, worthless metal—markets groaned.

sentences.zh: 權聞百姓不以為便，省息之，鑄為器物，官勿復出也。

translations.literal: When Quan heard commoners found it inconvenient he scaled it back, cast the metal into vessels, and ordered offices not to issue it again.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan melted the bubble coin into bronze ware and stopped minting.

sentences.zh: 私家有者，並以輸藏，平卑其直，勿有所枉。

translations.literal: Whatever private households held they were to surrender to storage at assessed fair value without cheating.
translations.idiomatic: Households redeemed hoards at fair melt weight.

sentences.zh: 晉自中原喪亂，元帝過江，用孫氏舊錢，輕重雜行，大者謂之比輪，中者謂之四文。

translations.literal: After Jin lost the central plain and Yuan Di crossed the Yangzi, they used Sun-era coinage with mixed weights: large pieces called 'paired disks,' middling ones called 'four-script.'
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin recycled Wu coin—large bi-lun disks and medium four-character pieces.

sentences.zh: 吳興沈充又鑄小錢，謂之沈郎錢。

translations.literal: Shen Chong of Wuxing also minted petty cash called Shen Lang coin.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxing's Shen Chong clipped 'Shen Lang' petty cash.

sentences.zh: 錢既不多，由是稍貴。

translations.literal: Because coin stayed scarce it gradually grew dear.
translations.idiomatic: Thin supply drove bronze dear.

sentences.zh: 孝武，詔曰：「錢，國之重寶，小人貪利，銷壞無已，監司當以為意。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict: 'Cash is the state's great treasure; petty men crave profit and melt it endlessly—inspectors must attend to this.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu warned against melting coin for scrap.

sentences.zh: 廣州夷人寶貴銅鼓，而州境素不出銅，聞官私賈人皆於此下貪比輪錢斤兩差重，以入廣州，貨與夷人，鑄敗作鼓。

translations.literal: 'Guangzhou tribes treasure bronze drums yet the canton yields little copper; rumor says official and private merchants buy overweight bi-lun coin here to ship into Guangzhou, vend it to tribes, and recast ruined drums.'
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese tribes prized drums—merchants exported heavy Wu coin south to melt into gongs.

sentences.zh: 其重為禁制，得者科罪。

translations.literal: 'Strictly forbid this; offenders face statutory punishment.'
translations.idiomatic: Ban drum smuggling under penalty.

sentences.zh: 」安帝元興中，桓玄輔政，立議欲廢錢用穀帛。

translations.literal: 'Under Emperor An's Yuanxing era Huan Xuan directed policy and proposed abolishing coin for grain and silk.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing regent Huan Xuan pushed grain-silk currency.

sentences.zh: 孔琳之議曰：

translations.literal: Kong Linzhi argued:
translations.idiomatic: Kong Linzhi rebutted him.

sentences.zh: 《洪範》八政，貨為食次，豈不以交易所資，為用之至要者乎！

translations.literal: 'The Hong Fan's eight policies place goods second to food—is it not because exchange supplies what use requires most!'
translations.idiomatic: Hong Fan ranks grain above currency.

sentences.zh: 若使百姓用力于為錢，則是妨為生之業，禁之可也。

translations.literal: 'If commoners were forced to labor at minting coin, that would obstruct livelihood—there one may forbid.'
translations.idiomatic: Ban mint labor if it steals farm time.

sentences.zh: 今農自務穀，工自務器，各隸其業，何嘗致勤于錢。

translations.literal: 'Now farmers pursue grain and artisans pursue tools—each sticks to his trade; none wastes sweat on coin.'
translations.idiomatic: Farmers and smiths never mined—they traded.

sentences.zh: 故聖王制無用之貨，以通有用之財，既無毀敗之費，又省難運之苦，此錢所以嗣功龜貝，歷代不廢者也。

translations.literal: 'Thus sage kings fashioned useless goods to circulate useful wealth—without destruction costs or punishing transport hardship—why coin succeeded shells and tortoise and endured every dynasty.'
translations.idiomatic: Coin replaced shells because it moved cheaply.

sentences.zh: 穀帛為寶，本充衣食，分以為貨，則致損甚多。

translations.literal: 'Grain and silk are treasures meant for clothing and food; split them into currency and damage multiplies.'
translations.idiomatic: Turning food bolts into cash ruins cloth.

sentences.zh: 又勞毀于商販之手，秏棄於割截之用，此之為弊，著自於曩。

translations.literal: 'They further labor under merchants' hands and waste in cutting pieces—those abuses appeared long ago.'
translations.idiomatic: Bolt currency shredded in merchants' claws.

sentences.zh: 故鐘繇曰，巧偽之人，競濕穀以要利，制薄絹以充資。

translations.literal: 'Hence Zhong Yao said crafty men raced to dampen grain for profit and weave thin tabby for capital.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao warned wet grain and gauze silk.

sentences.zh: 魏世制以嚴刑，弗能禁也。

translations.literal: 'Wei instituted harsh punishments yet could not forbid it.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei torture never stopped bolt fraud.

sentences.zh: 是以司馬芝以為用錢非徒豐國，亦所以省刑。

translations.literal: 'Therefore Sima Zhi held using coin not only enriched the state but also reduced punishments.'
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhi tied coin to lighter torture.

sentences.zh: 錢之不用，由於兵亂積久，自致於廢，有由而然，漢末是也。

translations.literal: 'Coin fell into disuse because warfare dragged on until natural lapse ended it—as at late Han.'
translations.idiomatic: War retired coin late Han—not policy genius.

sentences.zh: 今既用而廢之，則百姓頓亡其利。

translations.literal: 'Now that we use it yet abolish it, common people instantly lose its benefit.'
translations.idiomatic: Banning coin now strands savings.

sentences.zh: 今括囊天下之穀，以周天下之食，或倉廩充溢，或糧靡並儲，以相資通，則貧者仰富。

translations.literal: 'Suppose we tie up all grain under Heaven to feed all mouths—some granaries overflow while others lack—yet mutual aid through coin lets poor rely on rich.'
translations.idiomatic: Regional glut and dearth even out through cash markets.

sentences.zh: 致富之道，實假于錢，一朝斷之，便為棄物。

translations.literal: 'The path to wealth truly borrows coin; cut it once and goods become refuse.'
translations.idiomatic: Wealth rides bronze—cut it and savings rot.

sentences.zh: 是有錢無糧之人，皆坐而饑困，以此斷之，又立弊也。

translations.literal: 'Thus holders of coin without grain sit starving—abolishing coin establishes fresh harm.'
translations.idiomatic: Urban cash holders starve if grain alone trades.

sentences.zh: 且據今用錢之處，不以為貧，用穀之處，不以為富。

translations.literal: 'Moreover regions using coin do not therefore grow poor; regions using grain do not therefore grow rich.'
translations.idiomatic: Coin provinces aren't poorer than barter zones.

sentences.zh: 又人習來久，革之必惑。

translations.literal: 'Further custom ingrains habit—uprooting it breeds confusion.'
translations.idiomatic: Long habit resists currency shocks.

sentences.zh: 語曰，利不百，不易業，況又錢便於穀邪！

translations.literal: The proverb says: without hundredfold gain do not change occupation—how much less when coin proves handier than grain!'
translations.idiomatic: Proverbs demand hundredfold gain before switching trades—coin beats grain.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝時錢廢，穀用既久，不以便於人，乃舉朝大議。

translations.literal: 'Under Emperor Ming of Wei coin lapsed and grain trade lasted long until it harmed people—thereupon the whole court debated.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mingdi's grain era sparked court-wide remint debates.

sentences.zh: 精才達政之士莫不以宜復用錢，下無異情，朝無異論。

translations.literal: 'Talented statesmen unanimously urged restoring coin; none below objected, none above dissented.'
translations.idiomatic: Every minister voted bronze back.

sentences.zh: 彼尚舍穀帛而用錢，足以明穀帛之弊著於已誡也。

translations.literal: 'They nonetheless abandoned grain and silk for coin—proof grain-silk harm was obvious warning.'
translations.idiomatic: Their unanimous remint proved bolt-money failed.

sentences.zh: 世或謂魏氏不用錢久，積累巨萬，故欲行之，利公富國，斯殆不然。

translations.literal: 'Some say Wei hoarded coinless wealth so long they wished circulation to enrich the treasury—hardly true.'
translations.idiomatic: Gossip wrongly credits Wei greed for remint.

sentences.zh: 晉文後舅犯之謀，而先成季之信，以為雖有一時之勳，不如萬世之益。

translations.literal: 'Duke Wen of Jin afterward employed Uncle Fan's stratagem yet earlier rewarded Chengji's good faith—holding one campaign's exploit inferior to endless-age benefit.'
translations.idiomatic: Jin Wen honored lasting loyalty over quick raids—that framed their monetary ethics.

sentences.zh: 于時名賢在列，君子盈朝，大謀天下之利害，將定經國之要術。

translations.literal: 'At that time famed worthies filled the ranks; gentlemen packed court—great deliberations weighed empire-wide harm and benefit and settled fundamentals of statecraft.'
translations.idiomatic: That court weighed eternal policy—not petty mint profits.

sentences.zh: 若穀實便錢，義不昧當時之近利，而廢永用之通業，斷可知矣。

translations.literal: 'If grain truly beat coin, duty would not blind them to immediate profit and discard everlasting commerce—plain as bronze.'
translations.idiomatic: Had grain topped coin, sages would have kept barter.

sentences.zh: 斯實由困而思革，改而更張耳。

translations.literal: 'This truly stems from hardship prompting reform—changing course when squeezed.'
translations.idiomatic: They reminted from crisis, not whim.

sentences.zh: 近孝武之末，天下無事，時和年豐，百姓樂業，穀帛殷阜，幾乎家給人足，驗之實事，錢又不妨人也。

translations.literal: 'Near late Xiaowu's reign the realm was calm, seasons mild and harvests rich; common people prospered in their trades; grain and silk piled high until nearly every household had enough—fact proves coin harmed no one.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu's peace showed coin compatible with plenty.

sentences.zh: 頃兵革屢興，荒饉薦及，饑寒未振，實此之由。

translations.literal: 'Recently wars stack atop famine after famine; cold hunger unrest stems from this.'
translations.idiomatic: Today's want came from spears, not sycee.

sentences.zh: 公既援而拯之，大革視聽，弘敦本之教，明廣農之科，敬授人時，各從其業，遊蕩知反，務末自休，同以南畝競力，野無遺壤矣。

translations.literal: 'Your lordship already rescues and lifts them, greatly reforming sight and sound, spreading root-emphasizing instruction, clarifying broad-farming statutes, reverently handing seasons to men so each pursues his occupation; wanderers know to return and secondary pursuits rest—together they compete in southern fields until no acre lies waste.'
translations.idiomatic: You, Lord Huan, already preach husbandry—finish that before demonetizing.

sentences.zh: 於此以往，將升平必至，何衣食之足恤！

translations.literal: 'Beyond this, rising peace must arrive—why fret clothing and food!'
translations.idiomatic: Peace will fill bellies without banning coin.

sentences.zh: 愚謂救弊之術，無取于廢錢。

translations.literal: 'Your servant thinks healing these ills does not lie in abolishing coin.'
translations.idiomatic: Fix farms, not mints.

sentences.zh: 朝議多同琳之，故玄議不行。

translations.literal: Court opinion largely agreed with Linzhi; therefore Huan Xuan's proposal did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Linzhi won the hall; Huan Xuan's barter scheme died.
